title.zh: 卷一 魏本紀第一: 太祖道武帝 太宗明元帝
title.en: Volume 1 Wei Annals 1: Emperor Daowu, Emperor Mingyuan
title.raw: 卷一 魏本紀第一: 太祖道武帝 太宗明元帝 Volume 1 Wei Annals 1: Emperor Daowu, Emperor Mingyuan

sentences.zh: 太祖道武帝 太宗明元帝

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Emperor Daowu; Grand Successor Emperor Mingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu the Grand Progenitor; Emperor Mingyuan the Grand Successor.

sentences.zh: 魏之先，出自黃帝軒轅氏。

translations.literal: The Wei forebears came forth from the Yellow Emperor, the Xuan Yuan clan.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei line traced its descent to the Yellow Emperor Xuan Yuan.

sentences.zh: 黃帝子曰昌意，昌意之少子受封北國，有大鮮卑山，因以為號。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor's son was named Changyi; Changyi's youngest son received enfeoffment in the Northern Realm, where stood Great Xianbei Mountain, and from this they took their designation.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor's son Changyi had a youngest son enfeoffed in the northland; Great Xianbei Mountain gave the people their name.

sentences.zh: 其後世為君長，統幽都之北廣莫之野，畜牧遷徙，射獵為業，淳樸為俗，簡易為化，不為文字，刻木結繩而已。

translations.literal: Their descendants in generation after generation became chieftains, ruling the vast northern wastes beyond Youdu; they herded and migrated, took hunting as their livelihood, held simplicity as custom and ease as transformation, made no written characters, and kept records only by notching wood and tying knots.
translations.idiomatic: Generation after generation they ruled the far north beyond Youdu: pastoral wanderers who hunted for a living, cherished plain ways, shunned writing, and remembered the past only by notched wood and knotted cord.

sentences.zh: 時事遠近，人相傳授，如史官之紀錄焉。

translations.literal: Matters near and far in time were passed from person to person, like records kept by historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: Near events and distant ones alike were handed down mouth to mouth, much like an archivist's chronicle.

sentences.zh: 黃帝以土德王。

translations.literal: The Yellow Emperor took the throne by the virtue of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow Emperor reigned through the power of Earth.

sentences.zh: 北俗謂土為托，謂後為跋，故以為氏。

translations.literal: In northern custom soil was called tuo and rear was called ba; hence they took it as their clan name.
translations.idiomatic: Northern speech called earth tuo and “behind” ba, and from those words came the name Tuoba.

sentences.zh: 其裔始均，仕堯時，逐女魃于弱水，北人賴其勳，舜命為田祖。

translations.literal: Among their descendants was Shi Jun, who served in the age of Yao, drove the drought demon Ba to the Weak Waters, and for this merit the northerners relied on him; Shun appointed him ancestor of the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Their descendant Shi Jun served under Yao, drove the drought demon Ba beyond the Weak Waters, and won such gratitude from the north that Shun named him lord of the fields.

sentences.zh: 曆三代至秦、漢，獯鬻、獫狁、山戎、匈奴之屬，累代作害中州。

translations.literal: Through the Three Dynasties down to Qin and Han, the Xunyu, Xianyun, Shanrong, Xiongnu, and their kind raided the central lands generation after generation.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Dynasties through Qin and Han, Xiongnu and kindred peoples such as Xunyu, Xianyun, and Shanrong harried the heartland again and again.

sentences.zh: 而始均之裔不交南夏，是以載籍無聞。

translations.literal: Yet the line of Shi Jun did not mingle with the southern Xia, and so went unrecorded in written annals.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Jun's line kept apart from the southern realms, and therefore left no trace in the written histories.

sentences.zh: 積六七十代，至成皇帝諱毛立，統國三十六，大姓九十九，威振北方。

translations.literal: After sixty or seventy generations, Emperor Cheng, taboo name Mao, took the throne, ruling thirty-six states and ninety-nine great clans, his might shaking the north.
translations.idiomatic: Sixty or seventy generations later Emperor Cheng, whose taboo name was Mao, came to power over thirty-six domains and ninety-nine great clans, and his authority awed the north.

sentences.zh: 成帝崩，節皇帝貸立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Cheng died, Emperor Jie, taboo name Dai, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Emperor died; Jie Emperor, taboo name Dai, took the throne.

sentences.zh: 節帝崩，莊皇帝觀立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jie died, Emperor Zhuang, taboo name Guan, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Jie Emperor died; Zhuang Emperor, taboo name Guan, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 莊帝崩，明皇帝樓立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang died, Emperor Ming, taboo name Lou, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Emperor died; Ming Emperor, taboo name Lou, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，安皇帝越立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, Emperor An, taboo name Yue, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Emperor died; An Emperor, taboo name Yue, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 安帝崩，宣皇帝推寅立。

translations.literal: When Emperor An died, Emperor Xuan, taboo name Tuiyin, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: An Emperor died; Xuan Emperor, taboo name Tuiyin, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 宣帝南遷大澤，方千餘里，厥土昏冥沮洳，謀更南徙，未行而崩。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan moved south to the Great Marsh, a thousand li and more on a side; its soil was dim, wet, and boggy. He planned a further move southward, but before he could act he died.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan Emperor led his people south to the Great Marsh, more than a thousand li across, where the ground lay dark and sodden. He meant to push farther south, but died before the march began.

sentences.zh: 景皇帝利立。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing, taboo name Li, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Emperor, taboo name Li, came to the throne.

sentences.zh: 景帝崩，元皇帝俟立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Jing died, Emperor Yuan, taboo name Hou, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Emperor died; Yuan Emperor, taboo name Hou, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 元帝崩，和皇帝肆立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yuan died, Emperor He, taboo name Si, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Emperor died; He Emperor, taboo name Si, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 和帝崩，定皇帝機立。

translations.literal: When Emperor He died, Emperor Ding, taboo name Ji, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He Emperor died; Ding Emperor, taboo name Ji, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 定帝崩，僖皇帝蓋立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ding died, Emperor Xi, taboo name Gai, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Emperor died; Xi Emperor, taboo name Gai, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 僖帝崩，威皇帝儈立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xi died, Emperor Wei, taboo name Kuai, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Emperor died; Wei Emperor, taboo name Kuai, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 威帝崩，獻皇帝鄰立。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wei died, Emperor Xian, taboo name Lin, succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor died; Xian Emperor, taboo name Lin, succeeded.

sentences.zh: 時有神人，言此土荒遐，宜徙建都邑。

translations.literal: At that time a divine man said this land was remote and barren and that they ought to move and establish a capital.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit-man appeared and declared the country too desolate for a capital; they must migrate and build anew.

sentences.zh: 獻帝年老，乃以位授于聖武皇帝，命南移。

translations.literal: Xian Emperor was old; he therefore yielded the throne to the Holy Martial Emperor and ordered a move south.
translations.idiomatic: Xian Emperor, grown old, abdicated in favor of the Holy Martial Emperor and commanded the nation to move south.

sentences.zh: 山谷高深，九難八阻，於是欲止。

translations.literal: The valleys were deep, the mountains high, with nine hardships and eight barriers; thereupon they wished to halt.
translations.idiomatic: Deep gorges and towering ridges blocked the way at every turn, and the people longed to stop.

sentences.zh: 有神獸，似馬，其聲類牛，導引歷年乃出，始居匈奴故地。

translations.literal: A divine beast, horse-like, with a voice like an ox, led them on for years until they emerged and first settled in the former lands of the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: A spirit-beast resembling a horse but lowing like an ox guided them for years until they broke free and made their home in the old Xiongnu country.

sentences.zh: 其遷徙策略，多出宣、獻二帝，故時人並號曰推寅，蓋俗雲鑽研之義。

translations.literal: Most of their migration strategy came from Emperors Xuan and Xian; therefore people of the time jointly styled them Tuiyin, which in common speech carried the sense of careful study.
translations.idiomatic: The plans behind the great migration were chiefly those of Xuan and Xian Emperors, so contemporaries called them both Tuiyin, meaning in folk speech to probe and weigh matters closely.

sentences.zh: 聖武皇帝諱詰汾，嘗田於山澤，欻見輜軿自天而下。

translations.literal: The Holy Martial Emperor, taboo name Jiefen, was once hunting in mountains and marshes when suddenly he saw a covered carriage descend from heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Holy Martial Emperor Jiefen was hunting in the hills when a curtained carriage dropped out of the sky.

sentences.zh: 既至，見美婦人自稱天女，受命相偶。

translations.literal: When it arrived, he saw a beautiful woman who called herself a heavenly maiden and said she had received a mandate to become his consort.
translations.idiomatic: From it stepped a radiant woman who called herself a daughter of Heaven and said fate had joined her to him.

sentences.zh: 旦日請還，期年周時復會於此，言終而別。

translations.literal: At dawn she asked to return; when a full year had turned she would meet him again here; when her words were finished she departed.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak she begged leave to go, promising to return to the same place when the year had come full circle, and vanished.

sentences.zh: 及期，帝至先田處，果見天女，以所生男授帝，曰：「此君之子也，當世為帝王。

translations.literal: When the appointed time came, the Emperor came to the place of his former hunt and indeed saw the heavenly maiden; she handed the boy she had borne to the Emperor, saying, "This is your son; in his age he shall be emperor.
translations.idiomatic: At the appointed season the Emperor returned to the hunting ground and found the heavenly maiden, who placed the boy she had borne in his arms and said, "He is your son, and in his day he shall rule as emperor.

sentences.zh: 」語訖而去。

translations.literal: " When she had spoken, she departed.
translations.idiomatic: With that she was gone.

sentences.zh: 即始祖神元皇帝也。

translations.literal: This was the Progenitor, Emperor Shenyuan.
translations.idiomatic: That child was the Progenitor, Shenyuan Emperor.

sentences.zh: 故時人諺曰：「詰汾皇帝無婦家，力微皇帝無舅家。

translations.literal: Hence a saying of the time: "Emperor Jiefen has no wife's kin; Emperor Liwei has no mother's kin.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the proverb: "Jiefen Emperor had no in-laws; Liwei Emperor had no uncles on his mother's side.

sentences.zh: 」帝崩，神元皇帝立。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor died, Shenyuan Emperor succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When Holy Martial Emperor died, Shenyuan Emperor took the throne.

sentences.zh: 神元皇帝諱力微。

translations.literal: Shenyuan Emperor, taboo name Liwei.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyuan Emperor, whose taboo name was Liwei.

sentences.zh: 元年，歲在庚子，先是西部內侵，依于沒鹿回部大人竇賓。

translations.literal: In the first year, the year being gengzi, the western tribes had earlier invaded within and attached themselves to the great chief Dou Bin of the Moluhui tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In year one, a gengzi year, the western tribes had already pushed inward and attached themselves to Dou Bin, great chief of the Moluhui.

sentences.zh: 神元有雄傑之度，後與賓攻西部，賓軍敗，失馬步走，神元使以所乘駿馬給之。

translations.literal: Shenyuan possessed a heroic and outstanding measure; later he joined Bin in attacking the western tribes. Bin's army was defeated; he lost his horse and fled on foot. Shenyuan had him given the fine steed he himself was riding.
translations.idiomatic: Liwei was a man of heroic stature. Later he campaigned with Bin against the western tribes; when Bin's force broke and he fled on foot, Shenyuan gave him his own swift horse.

sentences.zh: 賓歸，求馬主，帝隱而不言。

translations.literal: Bin returned and sought the horse's owner; the Emperor concealed the matter and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Bin came home asking who owned the horse; the Emperor kept silent.

sentences.zh: 賓後知，大驚，將分國之半奉帝，帝不受，乃進其愛女。

translations.literal: When Bin later learned of it he was greatly astonished and was about to offer half the realm to the Emperor; the Emperor would not accept, and Bin thereupon presented his beloved daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the truth, Bin was astonished and offered half his domain; Shenyuan refused, so Bin gave him his beloved daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 賓猶思報恩，乃從帝所欲，徙所部北居長川。

translations.literal: Bin still wished to repay the kindness; he therefore did as the Emperor desired and moved his following north to dwell on the Long River.
translations.idiomatic: Still eager to repay the debt, Bin moved his people north to the Long River as Shenyuan wished.

sentences.zh: 積數年，舊部人咸來歸附。

translations.literal: After several years, the men of the old following all came to attach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the old tribesmen were flocking to his banner.

sentences.zh: 及賓臨終，戒其二子，使謹奉神元。

translations.literal: When Bin was near death he admonished his two sons to serve Shenyuan with care.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Bin charged his two sons to honor Shenyuan faithfully.

sentences.zh: 其子不從，乃陰謀逆。

translations.literal: His sons would not obey and secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: The sons disobeyed and plotted treason in secret.

sentences.zh: 帝召殺之，盡並其眾。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned and killed them, and wholly absorbed their following.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyuan had them summoned and executed, then absorbed all their people.

sentences.zh: 諸部大人悉服，控弦之士二十餘萬。

translations.literal: The great chiefs of all the tribes submitted; bowmen numbered more than two hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Every tribal chief submitted, and archers in his service passed two hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，遷於定襄之盛樂。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year he moved to Shengle in Dingxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In his thirty-ninth year he shifted the seat of rule to Shengle in Dingxiang commandery.

sentences.zh: 四月祭天，諸部君長皆來助祭，唯白部大人觀望不至。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he sacrificed to Heaven; chieftains of all the tribes came to assist in the rites, but the great chief of the Bai tribe held back and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he offered to Heaven, and tribal chiefs gathered for the rite, but the Bai chief stayed away.

sentences.zh: 征而戮之，遠近肅然。

translations.literal: He campaigned against and executed him; near and far grew sternly orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyuan marched against him, put him to death, and awe settled over every quarter.

sentences.zh: 帝乃告諸大人，為與魏和親計。

translations.literal: The Emperor then told the great men that he planned a marriage alliance with Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He told the tribal elders he intended to seek a marriage alliance with Wei.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，遣子文帝如魏，且觀風土。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year he sent his son, Emperor Wen, to Wei and also to observe its customs and soil.
translations.idiomatic: In his forty-second year he sent his son Wen Emperor to Wei to study its land and ways.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏景元二年也。

translations.literal: That year was the second year of Jingyuan in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: That year corresponded to the second year of Jingyuan in Wei.

sentences.zh: 文帝諱沙漠汗，以國太子留洛陽。

translations.literal: Wen Emperor, taboo name Shamohan, remained in Luoyang as the state's heir.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Emperor, taboo name Shamohan, stayed in Luoyang as hostage heir.

sentences.zh: 後文帝以神元春秋已高，求歸。

translations.literal: Later Wen Emperor, because Shenyuan's years were already advanced, requested to return.
translations.idiomatic: Later, seeing Shenyuan's great age, Shamohan asked leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝具禮護送。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin treated him with full rites and escorted him on his way.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin honored him with full ceremony and sent him homeward under escort.

sentences.zh: 五十六年，文帝復如晉，其冬還國。

translations.literal: In the fifty-sixth year Wen Emperor again went to Jin; that winter he returned to his state.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-sixth year he visited Jin again and came back that winter.

sentences.zh: 晉征北將軍衛瓘以文帝雄異，恐為後患，請留不遣。

translations.literal: Wei Guan, General Who Subdues the North of Jin, because Wen Emperor was formidable and strange, feared he would be a later trouble and requested that he be detained and not sent back.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's north-pacifying general Wei Guan, fearing Shamohan's formidable talent, asked that he be kept and not released.

sentences.zh: 復請以金錦賂國之大人，令致間隙。

translations.literal: He again requested that gold and brocade be used to bribe the great men of the state so as to sow divisions among them.
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed bribing the tribal great men with gold and brocade to set them at odds with one another.

sentences.zh: 五十八年方遣帝。

translations.literal: Only in the fifty-eighth year was the Emperor sent off.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the fifty-eighth year was the heir allowed to depart.

sentences.zh: 神元使諸部大人詣陰館迎帝。

translations.literal: Shenyuan had the great men of the tribes go to Yinyuan to welcome the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyuan ordered the tribal chiefs to Yinyuan to welcome the heir home.

sentences.zh: 酒酣，帝仰視飛鳥，飛丸落之。

translations.literal: As the wine went deep, the Emperor looked up at a flying bird and brought it down with a pellet.
translations.idiomatic: Wine deep in the cup, the heir glanced up at a bird in flight and dropped it with a pellet.

sentences.zh: 時國俗無彈，眾大驚，相謂曰：「太子被服同南夏，兼奇術絕人。

translations.literal: At the time the nation's custom knew no slings; all were greatly alarmed and said to one another, "The heir dresses like the southern Xia and possesses wondrous arts beyond any man.
translations.idiomatic: The people knew no slingshot; everyone was shaken and murmured, "The heir wears southern dress and commands arts no one here can match.

sentences.zh: 若繼國統，變易舊俗，吾等必不得志。

translations.literal: If he inherits the state and alters our old ways, we shall never have our will."
translations.idiomatic: If he inherits the realm and changes our customs, we will never prosper again."

sentences.zh: 」乃謀危害帝，並先馳還，曰：「太子引空弓而落飛鳥，似得晉人異法。

translations.literal: Thereupon they plotted to harm the Emperor, and first galloped back, saying, "The heir drew an empty bow yet brought down a flying bird, as though he had obtained some strange method of the Jin people.
translations.idiomatic: They plotted against him and rode ahead with a story: "The heir shot an empty bow and felled a bird in flight, as if he had learned some Jin sorcery.

sentences.zh: 」自帝在晉後，諸子愛寵，神元頗有所惑。

translations.literal: After the Emperor had been in Jin, the other sons were favored and cherished, and Shenyuan was much perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: During Shamohan's long stay in Jin, his younger brothers won favor, and Shenyuan grew uncertain.

sentences.zh: 及聞諸大人請，因曰：「當便除之。

translations.literal: On hearing the great men's request, he therefore said, "He should be removed at once.
translations.idiomatic: When the elders pressed their case, he said, "Then let him be killed at once.

sentences.zh: 」於是諸大人馳詣塞南，矯害帝。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the great men galloped to the south of the passes and, by forged command, killed the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: The great men raced south of the frontier passes and murdered the heir under a forged order.

sentences.zh: 其年，神元不豫。

translations.literal: In that year Shenyuan was unwell.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Shenyuan fell ill.

sentences.zh: 烏丸王庫賢親近任勢。

translations.literal: Kuxian, king of the Wuhuan, was close at hand and wielded power.
translations.idiomatic: Kuxian, a Wuhuan king, stood close to the throne and held real power.

sentences.zh: 先受衛瓘之貨，欲沮動諸部，因於庭中礪鉞斧，曰：「上恨汝曹讒殺太子，欲盡收諸大人長子殺之。

translations.literal: He had earlier accepted bribes from Wei Guan and wished to stir up the various tribes; therefore in the courtyard he sharpened axe and hatchet, saying, "The High One resents you all for slandering and killing the heir; he intends to seize every great man's eldest sons and put them to death.
translations.idiomatic: Having taken Wei Guan's bribes, he meant to panic the tribes; in the courtyard he sharpened axe and blade, crying, "The High One blames you for the heir's murder and will seize every chief's eldest son and kill him.

sentences.zh: 」大人皆信，各各散走。

translations.literal: " The great men all believed it; each scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs believed him and fled in every direction.

sentences.zh: 神元尋崩，凡饗國五十八年，年一百四歲。

translations.literal: Shenyuan soon died; in all he had ruled the state fifty-eight years, and his years reached one hundred and four.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyuan died soon after, having ruled fifty-eight years and lived to one hundred and four.

sentences.zh: 道武即位，尊為始祖。

translations.literal: When Daowu took the throne he honored him as Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Daowu came to power he enshrined Shenyuan as the dynastic Progenitor.

sentences.zh: 子章皇帝悉鹿立，時諸部離叛。

translations.literal: His son Zhang Emperor Silu succeeded; at the time the tribes were breaking away.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhang Emperor Silu succeeded while the tribes were splintering away.

sentences.zh: 帝九年而崩。

translations.literal: The Emperor died in the ninth year.
translations.idiomatic: Silu reigned nine years and died.

sentences.zh: 弟平皇帝綽立，七年而崩。

translations.literal: His younger brother Ping Emperor Chuo succeeded; in seven years he died.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Ping Emperor Chuo ruled seven years and died.

sentences.zh: 文帝少子思皇帝立，思皇帝諱弗。

translations.literal: The youngest son of Wen Emperor, Si Emperor, succeeded; Si Emperor, taboo name Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Emperor's youngest son, Si Emperor, came next; Si Emperor's taboo name was Fu.

sentences.zh: 政崇寬簡，百姓懷服。

translations.literal: His government honored leniency and simplicity; the common people were attached and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with leniency and ease, and the people gave him their hearts.

sentences.zh: 一年而崩。

translations.literal: In one year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died after a single year.

sentences.zh: 神元子昭帝祿官立。

translations.literal: Shenyuan's son Zhao Emperor Luguan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyuan's son Zhao Emperor Luguan took the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝元年，分國為三部：一居上穀北，濡源西，東接宇文部，自統之；

translations.literal: In the first year of the Emperor he divided the state into three parts: one group dwelt north of Shanggu, west of Ruyuan, bordering the Yuwen tribe, and he ruled them himself;
translations.idiomatic: In his first year Luguan split the realm in three: one branch lived north of Shanggu and west of Ruyuan, adjoining the Yuwen, under his own hand;

sentences.zh: 一居代郡之參合陂北，使文帝長子桓帝諱猗厓統之；

translations.literal: one dwelt north of Canhebo in Dai commandery, and he had Wen Emperor's eldest son Huan Emperor, taboo name Yiyu, rule them;
translations.idiomatic: one camped north of Canhe Marsh in Dai commandery, ruled by Wen Emperor's eldest son Huan Emperor, taboo name Yiyu;

sentences.zh: 一居定襄之盛樂故城，使桓帝弟穆帝猗盧統之。

translations.literal: one dwelt at the old city of Shengle in Dingxiang, and he had Huan Emperor's younger brother Mu Emperor Yilu rule them.
translations.idiomatic: one occupied old Shengle in Dingxiang, ruled by Huan Emperor's younger brother Mu Emperor Yilu.

sentences.zh: 自神元以來，與晉和好。

translations.literal: From Shenyuan's time onward they were on good terms with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: From Shenyuan's day the Tuoba had kept peace with Jin.

sentences.zh: 是歲，穆帝始出并州，遷雜胡北徙雲中、五原、朔方。

translations.literal: That year Mu Emperor first came out of Bing province, moving mixed barbarians northward into Yunzhong, Wuyuan, and Shuofang.
translations.idiomatic: That year Mu Emperor marched out of Bing province and shifted mixed tribes north into Yunzhong, Wuyuan, and Shuofang.

sentences.zh: 又西度河，擊匈奴、烏丸諸部。

translations.literal: He also crossed the river westward and struck the Xiongnu, Wuhuan, and other tribes.
translations.idiomatic: He also crossed the river west and attacked Xiongnu, Wuhuan, and other peoples.

sentences.zh: 自杏城以北八十里，迄長城原，夾道立碣，與晉分界。

translations.literal: From eighty li north of Xingcheng to the Yuan of the Long Wall, boundary markers were set along the road to divide the territory with Jin.
translations.idiomatic: From eighty li north of Xingcheng to the Long Wall plateau they set boundary stones along the road to mark the border with Jin.

sentences.zh: 二年，葬文帝及皇后封氏。

translations.literal: In the second year they buried Wen Emperor and Empress Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year they buried Wen Emperor and Empress Feng.

sentences.zh: 初，思帝欲改葬，未果而崩，至是述成前意焉。

translations.literal: Earlier Si Emperor had wished to rebury them but had not succeeded before he died; now he carried out the former intention.
translations.idiomatic: Si Emperor had meant to rebury them but died before he could; now Luguan fulfilled that wish.

sentences.zh: 三年，桓帝度漠北巡，因西略諸國，凡積五歲，諸部降附者三十餘國。

translations.literal: In the third year Huan Emperor crossed the desert on a northern tour and then campaigned west against the various states; in all for five years, more than thirty states submitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Huan Emperor toured north beyond the desert and campaigned west; over five years more than thirty peoples submitted.

sentences.zh: 桓帝英傑魁岸，馬不能勝，常乘安車，駕大牛，牛角容一石。

translations.literal: Huan Emperor was heroic, outstanding, and towering; horses could not bear him, and he often rode in a secure carriage drawn by great oxen, whose horns could hold a stone of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Emperor was a giant of heroic build whom horses could not carry; he often rode a secure cart pulled by oxen whose horns could hold a stone of grain.

sentences.zh: 帝曾中蠱，嘔吐之地仍生榆，參合陂土無榆，故時人異之。

translations.literal: The Emperor had once been struck by gu poison; where he vomited on the ground an elm tree grew, yet the soil of Canhebo had no elms, and therefore people of the time marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: Once poisoned, he vomited on the ground and an elm sprang up where none grew at Canhe Marsh, and people took it for a wonder.

sentences.zh: 十年，匈奴別種劉元海反晉于離石，自號漢王。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Liu Yuanhai, a separate branch of the Xiongnu, rebelled against Jin at Lishi and styled himself King of Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Liu Yuanhai, a Xiongnu offshoot, rose against Jin at Lishi and proclaimed himself King of Han.

sentences.zh: 并州刺史司馬騰來乞師，桓帝與帝大舉以助之，大破元海眾於西河、上黨。

translations.literal: Bing province inspector Sima Teng came to beg troops; Huan Emperor and the Emperor raised a great force to aid him and greatly defeated Yuanhai's host at Xihe and Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: Bing inspector Sima Teng asked for aid; Huan and Zhao Emperors marched in force and routed Yuanhai's army at Xihe and Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 桓帝與騰盟於汾東而還，乃使輔相衛雄、段繁，於參合陂西累石為亭，樹碑以記行焉。

translations.literal: Huan Emperor allied with Teng east of the Fen and returned; he then sent the assisting ministers Wei Xiong and Duan Fan west of Canhebo to pile stones into a pavilion and set up a stele to record the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Emperor joined Teng in alliance east of the Fen, then sent ministers Wei Xiong and Duan Fan to pile stones into a pavilion west of Canhe Marsh and raise a stele to commemorate the march.

sentences.zh: 十一年，晉假桓帝大單于金印紫綬。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year Jin invested Huan Emperor as Grand Chanyu with a golden seal and purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Jin granted Huan Emperor the title Grand Chanyu with a golden seal and purple cord.

sentences.zh: 是歲，桓帝崩。

translations.literal: In that year Huan Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: That year Huan Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 桓帝統部凡十一年。

translations.literal: In all Huan Emperor ruled his division eleven years.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Emperor had ruled his division for eleven years in all.

sentences.zh: 後定襄侯衛操樹碑於大邗城，以頌功德。

translations.literal: Later, Dingxiang Marquis Wei Cao erected a stele at Dahang City to praise his merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Later Dingxiang Marquis Wei Cao raised a stele at Dahang City to celebrate his achievements.

sentences.zh: 子普根代立。

translations.literal: His son Pugen succeeded in his place.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pugen took his place as chief.

sentences.zh: 十三年，昭帝崩。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Zhao Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Zhao Emperor died.

sentences.zh: 穆帝遂總攝三部為一統。

translations.literal: Mu Emperor thereupon took overall charge of the three divisions and made them one rule.
translations.idiomatic: Mu Emperor then gathered the three divisions under a single rule.

sentences.zh: 帝天姿英峙，勇略過人。

translations.literal: The Emperor was gifted by Heaven with heroic stature; his courage and strategy surpassed other men.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven had given him a heroic bearing and a courage and cunning that outmatched any rival.

sentences.zh: 元年，劉元海僭帝號，自稱大漢。

translations.literal: In the first year Liu Yuanhai usurped an imperial title and styled himself Great Han.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year Liu Yuanhai seized an imperial title and proclaimed the Great Han.

sentences.zh: 三年，晉并州刺史劉琨遣子遵為質，乞師。

translations.literal: In the third year Liu Kun, Jin inspector of Bing province, sent his son Zun as hostage and begged for troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Liu Kun of Bing province sent his son Zun as hostage and asked for military aid.

sentences.zh: 帝使弟子平文皇帝助琨，破白部大人，次攻鐵弗劉武。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent his younger brother's son, Emperor Pingwen, to aid Kun, defeated the White Tribe great chief, and next attacked the Iron-Fu Liu Wu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent his nephew Pingwen Emperor to help Kun, routed the White Tribe chief, then marched against the Iron-Fu leader Liu Wu.

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝進帝大單于，封代公。

translations.literal: Emperor Huai of Jin advanced the Emperor to Grand Chanyu and enfeoffed him as Duke of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's Emperor Huai promoted him to Grand Chanyu and enfeoffed him as Duke of Dai.

sentences.zh: 帝以封邑去國縣遠，從琨求句注陘北地。

translations.literal: Because his fief lay far from the state capital, the Emperor asked Kun for the lands north of Gouzhu Pass.
translations.idiomatic: His grant lay too far from the heartland, so he asked Kun for territory north of Gouzhu Pass.

sentences.zh: 琨大喜，乃徙馬邑、陰館、樓煩、繁畤、崞五縣人于陘南，更立城邑，盡獻其地。

translations.literal: Kun was greatly pleased and therefore moved the people of Mayi, Yinyuan, Loufan, Fanchi, and Guo five commanderies south of the pass, rebuilt their towns, and presented all the land.
translations.idiomatic: Kun gladly moved the populations of Mayi, Yinyuan, Loufan, Fanchi, and Guo south of the pass, rebuilt their towns, and ceded the vacated lands in full.

sentences.zh: 東接代郡，西連西河、朔方數百百。

translations.literal: To the east it adjoined Dai commandery; to the west it linked with Xihe and Shuofang for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: It reached east to Dai commandery and west through Xihe and Shuofang for several hundred li.

sentences.zh: 帝乃徙十萬家以充之。

translations.literal: The Emperor then moved a hundred thousand households to fill it.
translations.idiomatic: He then settled a hundred thousand households there to people the land.

sentences.zh: 六年，城盛樂以為北都，修故平城以為南都。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he walled Shengle as the northern capital and restored old Pingcheng as the southern capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he fortified Shengle as the northern capital and restored old Pingcheng as the southern capital.

sentences.zh: 帝登平城西山，觀望地勢，乃更南百里，于氵壘水之陽黃瓜堆築新平城，晉人謂之小平城。

translations.literal: The Emperor climbed the western hills of Pingcheng, surveyed the terrain, and therefore moved a further hundred li south to build a new Pingcheng on the south bank of the Luo River at Huangguadui; Jin people called it Little Pingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: From the western hills of Pingcheng he studied the ground, then shifted south another hundred li to build New Pingcheng on the south bank of the Luo at Huangguadui, which Jin subjects called Little Pingcheng.

sentences.zh: 使子六修鎮之，統領南部。

translations.literal: He had his son Liuxiu garrison it and take overall charge of the southern lands.
translations.idiomatic: He stationed his son Liuxiu there to command the southern territories.

sentences.zh: 八年，晉湣帝進帝為代王，置官屬，食代、常山二郡。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Emperor Min of Jin advanced the Emperor to King of Dai, established an official staff, and granted the revenues of Dai and Changshan commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Jin's Emperor Min raised him to King of Dai with a full bureaucracy and the income of Dai and Changshan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 先是國俗寬簡，至是明刑峻法，諸部人多以違命得罪。

translations.literal: Earlier the national custom had been broad and simple; now clear laws and stern punishments were enforced, and many men of the various tribes were condemned for disobeying orders.
translations.idiomatic: Where the nation had once been easygoing, he now imposed sharp law; tribesmen fell in numbers for defying his commands.

sentences.zh: 凡後期者皆舉部戮之，或有室家相攜，悉赴死所。

translations.literal: All who were late were put to death with their whole tribe, and sometimes whole households went together, all heading for the place of execution.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who missed a deadline died with his entire clan, and whole families sometimes walked to the killing ground hand in hand.

sentences.zh: 人問何之，曰當就誅。

translations.literal: When people asked where they were going, they said, "We are going to be executed."
translations.idiomatic: Asked where they were bound, they answered, "To be put to death."

sentences.zh: 其威嚴若此。

translations.literal: His stern majesty was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the terror of his rule.

sentences.zh: 九年，帝召六修不至，怒，討之失利，遂崩。

translations.literal: In the ninth year the Emperor summoned Liuxiu, but he did not come; enraged, the Emperor campaigned against him, met defeat, and thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he summoned Liuxiu; when the prince refused to come, the King marched against him, lost the fight, and died.

sentences.zh: 普根先守外境，聞難，來攻六修滅之。

translations.literal: Pugen had earlier guarded the outer marches; on hearing of the crisis he came, attacked Liuxiu, and destroyed him.
translations.idiomatic: Pugen, who had been guarding the frontier, heard the news, marched in, attacked Liuxiu, and wiped him out.

sentences.zh: 普根立月餘薨。

translations.literal: Pugen reigned a little more than a month and died.
translations.idiomatic: Pugen ruled barely a month before he died.

sentences.zh: 普根子始生，桓帝后立之，又薨，思帝子平文皇帝立。

translations.literal: Pugen's son had just been born; Huan Emperor's consort installed him, but he too died; then Si Emperor's son, Emperor Pingwen, was raised to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Pugen's infant son was set up by Huan Emperor's widow, but he soon died as well, and Si Emperor's son Pingwen Emperor took the throne.

sentences.zh: 平文皇帝諱郁律，姿質雄壯，甚有威略。

translations.literal: Emperor Pingwen, taboo name Yulü, was of heroic and stalwart bearing and possessed great authority and strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Pingwen Emperor, taboo name Yulü, was powerfully built and commanded awe through force and guile.

sentences.zh: 元年，歲在丁丑。

translations.literal: In the first year the year was dingchou.
translations.idiomatic: His first year was a dingchou year.

sentences.zh: 二年，劉武據朔方，來侵西部，帝大破之。

translations.literal: In the second year Liu Wu held Shuofang, came to invade the western lands, and the Emperor routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Liu Wu, entrenched in Shuofang, invaded the west and was shattered.

sentences.zh: 西兼烏孫故地，東吞勿吉以西，控弦上馬將百萬。

translations.literal: To the west he annexed the old lands of the Wusun; to the east he swallowed all west of the Wuji; bowmen and mounted warriors numbered a million.
translations.idiomatic: He seized the old Wusun country in the west and swallowed everything west of the Wuji in the east; a million warriors stood ready at bow and saddle.

sentences.zh: 是歲，晉元帝即位于江南，劉曜僭帝位。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Yuan of Jin took the throne in the southland, and Liu Yao usurped an imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: That year Jin's Emperor Yuan reigned south of the Yangtze while Liu Yao claimed the imperial dignity.

sentences.zh: 帝聞晉湣帝為曜所害，顧謂大臣曰：「今中原無主，天其資我乎。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard that Emperor Min of Jin had been killed by Yao, he turned to his ministers and said, "Now the central lands have no lord; has Heaven perhaps endowed us?"
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Liu Yao had killed Emperor Min, he told his ministers, "The heartland is masterless. Has Heaven chosen us?"

sentences.zh: 」曜遣使請和，帝不納。

translations.literal: Yao sent envoys to sue for peace, but the Emperor would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yao sent envoys seeking peace; the Emperor refused them.

sentences.zh: 三年，石勒自稱趙王，遣使乞和，請為兄弟，帝斬其使以絕之。

translations.literal: In the third year Shi Le styled himself King of Zhao, sent envoys to beg peace and ask to be brothers; the Emperor beheaded his envoys to break off relations.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Shi Le proclaimed himself King of Zhao and sent envoys offering brotherhood; the Emperor executed them and broke off ties.

sentences.zh: 五年，晉元帝遣使韓暢加崇爵服，帝絕之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Emperor Yuan of Jin sent the envoy Han Chang to add noble rank and robes of honor; the Emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Jin's Emperor Yuan sent Han Chang with titles and regalia; the Emperor turned him away.

sentences.zh: 講武，有平南夏志。

translations.literal: He held martial reviews and harbored the will to pacify the southern Xia.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled his armies and burned to pacify the southern realms.

sentences.zh: 桓帝后以帝得眾心，恐不利己子，害帝，遂崩，大人死者數十人。

translations.literal: Huan Emperor's consort, because the Emperor had won the people's hearts and she feared harm to her own son, killed the Emperor; several tens of great chiefs died as well.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his popularity would endanger her son, Huan Emperor's widow murdered him, and dozens of tribal chiefs died in the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 天興初，追尊曰太祖。

translations.literal: At the opening of Tianxing he was posthumously honored as Grand Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: When Tianxing began he was enshrined posthumously as the Grand Progenitor.

sentences.zh: 桓帝中子惠帝賀傉立，以五年為元年。

translations.literal: Huan Emperor's second son, Emperor Hui Helu, succeeded and took the fifth year as his first.
translations.idiomatic: Huan Emperor's second son Hui Emperor Helu took the throne, dating his reign from the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 帝未親政事，太后臨朝。

translations.literal: The Emperor did not yet handle government in person; the empress dowager held court.
translations.idiomatic: The young king did not yet rule; the empress dowager governed.

sentences.zh: 遣使與石勒通和，時人謂之女國使。

translations.literal: She sent envoys to open relations with Shi Le, and people of the time called them the envoys of the women's state.
translations.idiomatic: She sent envoys to Shi Le, whom contemporaries nicknamed the ambassadors of the women's court.

sentences.zh: 四年，帝始臨朝，以諸部人情未悉款順，乃築城於東木根山，徙都之。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the Emperor first held court in person; because the hearts of the various tribes were not yet fully loyal, he walled a city on East Mugen Mountain and moved the capital there.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he took the throne in person; doubting tribal loyalty, he built a fortress on East Mugen Mountain and moved the seat of rule there.

sentences.zh: 五年，帝崩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Emperor died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 弟煬帝紇那立，以五年為元年。

translations.literal: His younger brother, Emperor Yang Henai, succeeded and took the fifth year as his first.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Yang Emperor Henai succeeded, again dating from the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 三年，石勒遣石季龍寇邊部，帝御之，不利，遷於大寧。

translations.literal: In the third year Shi Le sent Shi Jilong to raid the borderlands; the Emperor met him in battle, fared ill, and moved to Daning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Shi Le sent Shi Jilong against the frontier; defeated, the Emperor withdrew to Daning.

sentences.zh: 時平文帝長子烈帝居於舅賀蘭部，帝遣使求之，賀蘭部帥藹頭擁護不遣。

translations.literal: At that time Pingwen Emperor's eldest son, Emperor Lie, dwelt with his maternal uncles in the Helan tribe; the Emperor sent envoys to demand him, but Helan chief Aitou shielded him and would not send him.
translations.idiomatic: Pingwen Emperor's eldest son Lie Emperor lived then with his Helan kinsmen; envoys demanded his return, but chief Aitou refused to surrender him.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，召宇文部並力擊藹頭。

translations.literal: The Emperor was enraged and summoned the Yuwen tribe to join forces and strike Aitou.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, he called in the Yuwen and marched against Aitou.

sentences.zh: 宇文眾敗，帝還大寧。

translations.literal: The Yuwen host was defeated, and the Emperor returned to Daning.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuwen were beaten and the Emperor fell back to Daning.

sentences.zh: 五年，帝出居於宇文部，賀蘭及諸部大人共立烈帝。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the Emperor went out to dwell with the Yuwen tribe; Helan and the great chiefs of the tribes jointly installed Lie Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he took refuge with the Yuwen while Helan and the other chiefs raised Lie Emperor.

sentences.zh: 烈皇帝諱翳槐，以五年為元年。

translations.literal: Lie Emperor, taboo name Yihuai, took the fifth year as his first.
translations.idiomatic: Lie Emperor, taboo name Yihuai, began his reign from the fifth year.

sentences.zh: 石勒遣使求和，帝遣弟昭成帝如襄國，徙者五千餘家。

translations.literal: Shi Le sent envoys to sue for peace; the Emperor sent his younger brother, Emperor Zhaocheng, to Xiangguo, and more than five thousand households moved there.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Le sued for peace; the Emperor sent his brother Zhaocheng Emperor to Xiangguo, and more than five thousand families went with him.

sentences.zh: 七年，藹頭不修臣職，召而戮之，國人復貳。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Aitou failed in his duties as subject; the Emperor summoned and executed him, and the people again grew divided.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Aitou neglected his obligations; summoned and killed, he left the realm divided once more.

sentences.zh: 於是煬帝自宇文部還入，諸部大人復奉之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yang Emperor returned from the Yuwen tribe, and the great chiefs of the tribes again supported him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Emperor came back from the Yuwen, and the tribal chiefs rallied to him again.

sentences.zh: 煬帝以烈帝七年為後元年。

translations.literal: Yang Emperor took Lie Emperor's seventh year as the first year of the latter reign.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Emperor reckoned Lie Emperor's seventh year as the opening of a new era.

sentences.zh: 時烈帝出居於鄴。

translations.literal: At that time Lie Emperor was living in exile at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Lie Emperor then dwelt in exile at Ye.

sentences.zh: 三年，石季龍納烈帝於大寧。

translations.literal: In the third year Shi Jilong brought Lie Emperor into Daning.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Shi Jilong installed Lie Emperor at Daning.

sentences.zh: 國人六千餘家部落叛，煬帝出居於慕容部。

translations.literal: More than six thousand households and tribes rebelled; Yang Emperor went out to dwell with the Murong tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Six thousand-odd families rebelled, and Yang Emperor took refuge with the Murong.

sentences.zh: 烈帝復立，以煬帝三年為後元年。

translations.literal: Lie Emperor was restored and took Yang Emperor's third year as the first year of the latter reign.
translations.idiomatic: Lie Emperor was restored and dated a new era from Yang Emperor's third year.

sentences.zh: 城盛樂城，在故城東南十里。

translations.literal: He walled Shengle city, ten li southeast of the old city.
translations.idiomatic: He built Shengle city ten li southeast of the old capital.

sentences.zh: 一年而崩。

translations.literal: After one year he died.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he died.

sentences.zh: 弟昭成皇帝立。

translations.literal: His younger brother Emperor Zhaocheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Zhaocheng Emperor took the throne.

sentences.zh: 昭成皇帝諱什翼犍，平文皇帝之次子也。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaocheng, taboo name Shiyijian, was the second son of Emperor Pingwen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng Emperor, taboo name Shiyijian, was Pingwen Emperor's second son.

sentences.zh: 生而奇偉，寬仁大度。

translations.literal: From birth he was marvelously grand, broad in kindness and great in magnanimity.
translations.idiomatic: He was born strange and splendid, generous of heart and vast in spirit.

sentences.zh: 身長八尺，隆准龍顏，立發委地，臥則乳垂至席。

translations.literal: He stood eight feet tall, with a lofty nose and dragon countenance; standing, his hair trailed to the ground; lying down, his breasts hung to the mat.
translations.idiomatic: Eight feet tall, with a high-bridged nose and dragon face, his hair swept the floor when he stood and his breasts reached the mat when he lay down.

sentences.zh: 烈帝臨崩，顧命迎帝，曰：「立此人則社稷乃安。

translations.literal: As Lie Emperor neared death he charged that the Emperor be welcomed, saying, "If you install this man the altars will be secure."
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Lie Emperor ordered the court to fetch Shiyijian, saying, "Set this man on the throne and the realm will stand firm."

sentences.zh: 」故帝弟孤自詣鄴奉迎，與帝俱還。

translations.literal: Therefore the Emperor's younger brother Gu went in person to Ye to welcome him, and together they returned.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Gu went to Ye in person to escort him home.

sentences.zh: 建國元年十一月，帝即位於繁畤北，時年十九。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the first year of Jianguo the Emperor took the throne north of Fanchi; he was nineteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Jianguo year one he was enthroned north of Fanchi, aged nineteen.

sentences.zh: 二年春，始置百官，分掌眾職。

translations.literal: In the second spring he first established the hundred offices and divided the multitude of duties.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the second year he created the hundred offices and assigned their duties.

sentences.zh: 東自氵歲貊，西及破落那，莫不款附。

translations.literal: From the Sushen Mohe in the east to Poluona in the west, none failed to submit in good faith.
translations.idiomatic: From the eastern Sushen Mohe to western Poluona, every people came in loyal submission.

sentences.zh: 五月，朝諸大人于參合陂，議定都氵壘源川，連日不決，乃從太后計而止。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he held court with the great chiefs at Canhe Marsh to deliberate fixing the capital on the Luo source stream; for days they could not decide, and therefore they followed the empress dowager's plan and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the chiefs met at Canhe Marsh to debate a capital on the Luo headwaters; after days of deadlock they accepted the empress dowager's counsel and abandoned the move.

sentences.zh: 娉慕容晃妹為皇后。

translations.literal: He took Murong Huang's younger sister as empress.
translations.idiomatic: He married Murong Huang's younger sister as empress.

sentences.zh: 三年春，移都雲中之盛樂宮。

translations.literal: In the third spring he moved the capital to the Shengle Palace in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the third year he shifted the capital to the Shengle Palace at Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 四年，築盛樂城于故城南八里。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he built Shengle city eight li south of the old city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he built Shengle city eight li south of the old walls.

sentences.zh: 皇后慕容氏崩。

translations.literal: Empress Murong died.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Murong died.

sentences.zh: 十月，劉武寇西境，帝遣軍大破之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Liu Wu raided the western border; the Emperor sent troops and routed him utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Liu Wu struck the western frontier; the Emperor's army crushed him.

sentences.zh: 武死，子務桓立，始來歸順，帝以女妻之。

translations.literal: Wu died; his son Wuhuan succeeded and first came to submit; the Emperor gave him a daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Wu died and his son Wuhuan submitted; the Emperor gave him a princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 七年二月，遣大人長孫秩迎後慕容氏于和龍。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventh year he sent the great chief Zhangsun Zhi to welcome the later Empress Murong from Helong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventh year he sent chief Zhangsun Zhi to Helong to escort the new Murong empress.

sentences.zh: 晃送女於境。

translations.literal: Huang escorted the girl to the border.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Huang brought her to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 七月，慕容晃遣使來聘，求交婚。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Murong Huang sent envoys to propose a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Murong Huang sent envoys seeking kinship by marriage.

sentences.zh: 帝許之，以烈帝女妻焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor consented and gave him Lie Emperor's daughter as wife.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed and gave him Lie Emperor's daughter as bride.

sentences.zh: 十四年，帝以中州紛梗，將親率六軍，乘石氏之亂，廓定中原。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, because the central provinces were torn by disorder, the Emperor intended to lead the six armies in person, seize the chaos of the Shi clan, and pacify the central lands.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, with the heartland in turmoil, he meant to lead the six armies south, exploit the Shi clan's collapse, and conquer the central plains.

sentences.zh: 諸大人諫，乃止。

translations.literal: The great chiefs remonstrated, and he thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The tribal chiefs dissuaded him, and he abandoned the plan.

sentences.zh: 十八年，太后王氏崩。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year Empress Dowager Wang died.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year Empress Dowager Wang died.

sentences.zh: 十九年正月，劉務桓死，其弟閼頭立，潛謀反。

translations.literal: In the first month of the nineteenth year Liu Wuhuan died; his younger brother Kentou succeeded and secretly plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year's first month Liu Wuhuan died; his brother Kentou took power and plotted treason in secret.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，閼頭部人多叛，懼而東走，度河半濟而冰陷。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year most of Kentou's tribesmen rebelled; in fear he fled east, and when he was halfway across the river the ice gave way beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Kentou's people rose; fleeing east, he drowned halfway across the river when the ice broke.

sentences.zh: 後眾盡歸其兄子悉勿祈。

translations.literal: Later the multitude all returned to his elder brother's son Xiwuqi.
translations.idiomatic: In time the whole following passed to his nephew Xiwuqi.

sentences.zh: 初，閼頭之叛，悉勿祈兄弟十二人在帝左右，盡遣之歸，欲其自相猜離。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Kentou rebelled, Xiwuqi and his eleven brothers were at the Emperor's side; the Emperor sent them all home, wishing them to suspect and divide one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Kentou first rebelled, Xiwuqi and eleven brothers had been at court; the Emperor sent them all home hoping they would tear one another apart.

sentences.zh: 至是，悉勿祈奪其眾，閼頭窮而歸命，帝待之如初。

translations.literal: By then Xiwuqi had seized Kentou's following; Kentou, reduced to extremity, came to submit, and the Emperor treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Xiwuqi had by then stolen Kentou's host; Kentou, ruined, surrendered, and the Emperor received him as of old.

sentences.zh: 二十二年春，帝東巡桑乾川。

translations.literal: In the spring of the twenty-second year the Emperor toured east along the Sanggan River.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the twenty-second year he toured east along the Sanggan.

sentences.zh: 四月，悉勿祈死，弟衛辰立。

translations.literal: In the fourth month Xiwuqi died, and his younger brother Weichen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Xiwuqi died; his brother Weichen took his place.

sentences.zh: 二十三年六月，皇后慕容氏崩。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the twenty-third year Empress Murong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the twenty-third year Empress Murong died.

sentences.zh: 七月，衛辰來會葬，因求婚，許之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Weichen came to attend the funeral and thereupon asked for a marriage; the Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Weichen came to the funeral and asked for a bride; the Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，帝南巡君子津。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year the Emperor toured south to Junzi Ford.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he toured south as far as Junzi Ford.

sentences.zh: 二十八年正月，衛辰謀反，度河東。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year Weichen plotted rebellion and crossed east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twenty-eighth year Weichen rebelled and crossed east of the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 帝討之。

translations.literal: The Emperor campaigned against him.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor marched against him.

sentences.zh: 衛辰懼，遁走。

translations.literal: Weichen was afraid and fled in flight.
translations.idiomatic: Weichen fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 三十年十月，帝征衛辰。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the thirtieth year the Emperor campaigned against Weichen.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the thirtieth year he marched against Weichen.

sentences.zh: 時河冰未成，帝乃以葦絙約澌。

translations.literal: At that time the river ice had not yet formed; the Emperor therefore bound the floes with reed ropes.
translations.idiomatic: The river had not yet frozen, so he lashed the floes together with reed ropes.

sentences.zh: 俄然冰合，乃散葦於上，冰草相結若浮橋，眾軍利涉。

translations.literal: Suddenly the ice joined; he then scattered reeds on top, and ice and grass bound together like a floating bridge, so the army crossed with ease.
translations.idiomatic: Ice formed overnight; he spread reeds across it until ice and stalks knit into a bridge, and the army crossed with ease.

sentences.zh: 衛辰與宗族西走，收其部落而還。

translations.literal: Weichen fled west with his clansmen; the Emperor gathered in his tribes and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Weichen fled west with his kin; the Emperor gathered the tribes and turned home.

sentences.zh: 三十四年春，長孫斤謀反，伏誅。

translations.literal: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Zhangsun Jin plotted rebellion and was executed where he lay concealed.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the thirty-fourth year Zhangsun Jin rose in rebellion and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 斤之反也，拔刃向御坐。

translations.literal: When Jin rebelled, he drew his blade toward the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin rose in revolt, he bared his sword against the throne.

sentences.zh: 太子寔格之，傷肋，五月薨。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Shi intercepted him, was wounded in the ribs, and died in the fifth month.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Shi blocked him, took a wound in the ribs, and died that fifth month.

sentences.zh: 後追諡焉，是為獻明皇帝。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed and is known as Emperor Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: Later he received a posthumous title and is remembered as Emperor Xianming.

sentences.zh: 七月，皇孫珪生，大赦。

translations.literal: In the seventh month the imperial grandson Gui was born, and a general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month imperial grandson Gui was born and the realm was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 三十九年，苻堅遣其大司馬苻洛帥眾二十萬及其將硃彤、張蠔、鄧羌等諸道來寇，王師不利。

translations.literal: In the thirty-ninth year Fu Jian sent his Grand Marshal Fu Luo at the head of two hundred thousand men, with his generals Zhu Tong, Zhang Hao, Deng Qiang, and others coming by several routes to invade; the royal army fared ill.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-ninth year Fu Jian sent Grand Marshal Fu Luo with two hundred thousand troops and generals Zhu Tong, Zhang Hao, and Deng Qiang against the state by several roads; the royal army suffered defeat.

sentences.zh: 帝時不豫，乃率國人避於陰山之北。

translations.literal: The Emperor was then unwell and therefore led his people to shelter north of Yinshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was ill and led the nation north of Yinshan to escape.

sentences.zh: 高車雜種盡叛，四面寇抄，不得芻牧，復度漠南。

translations.literal: The mixed tribes of the Gaoche all rebelled; raiders struck on every side, fodder could not be gathered, and he crossed the desert south again.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoche tribes rose on every hand, raiders closed in from all quarters, and with no pasture for the herds he crossed the desert south once more.

sentences.zh: 堅軍稍退，乃還。

translations.literal: Jian's army gradually withdrew, and he then returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian's army drew back, he returned home.

sentences.zh: 十二月，至雲中。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he reached Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he reached Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 旬有二日，皇子寔君作亂。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day of the month Prince Shijun rose in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day Prince Shijun rebelled.

sentences.zh: 帝暴崩，時年五十七。

translations.literal: The Emperor died suddenly; he was fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor died suddenly at fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 道武即位，尊曰高祖。

translations.literal: When Daowu took the throne he honored him as High Progenitor.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu came to power and enshrined him as High Progenitor.

sentences.zh: 帝性寬厚。

translations.literal: The Emperor was by nature generous and mild.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was generous by nature.

sentences.zh: 時國少繒帛，代人許謙盜絹二疋，守者以告，帝匿之，謂燕鳳曰：「吾不忍視謙之面，卿勿泄之。

translations.literal: At that time the state had little silk; a man of the tribes named Xu Qian stole two bolts, and when the guard reported it the Emperor concealed the matter and said to Yan Feng, "I cannot bear to look upon Qian's face; do not reveal this.
translations.idiomatic: Silk was scarce in the realm when Xu Qian of the tribes stole two bolts; the guard told the Emperor, who hid the crime and said to Yan Feng, "I cannot bear to see Qian's face. Do not speak of this.

sentences.zh: 謙或慚而自殺，為財辱士，非也。

translations.literal: If Qian should die of shame by his own hand, that would be to disgrace a gentleman for mere goods, and that would be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: If shame drove Qian to kill himself, a man of worth would die for money, and that would be wrong.

sentences.zh: 」帝嘗擊西部叛賊，流矢中目。

translations.literal: Once, when the Emperor was striking rebel bandits in the western marches, a stray arrow struck his eye.
translations.idiomatic: Once, campaigning against western rebels, a stray arrow struck his eye.

sentences.zh: 賊破後，諸大臣執射者，各持錐刀欲屠割之。

translations.literal: After the bandits were broken, the great ministers seized the archer; each took awl and knife, eager to carve him apart.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels were crushed, ministers seized the archer, awls and knives in hand, ready to butcher him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「各為其主，何罪也，釋之！

translations.literal: The Emperor said, "Each served his own lord; what crime is that? Release him!
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Each man served his own lord. What crime is that? Let him go!

sentences.zh: 」其仁恕若此。

translations.literal: Such was his mercy and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the mercy of his rule.

sentences.zh: 太祖道武皇帝諱珪，昭成皇帝之嫡孫，獻明帝之子也。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Emperor Daowu, taboo name Gui, was the eldest son's son of Zhaocheng Emperor and the son of Emperor Xianming.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Emperor Daowu, taboo name Gui, was Zhaocheng Emperor's grandson by the direct line and the son of Emperor Xianming.

sentences.zh: 母曰獻明賀皇后，初因遷徙，游於雲澤。

translations.literal: His mother was Empress He of Xianming; in the first days of the migration she traveled to Yun Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Empress He of Xianming; during the early migrations she came to Yun Marsh.

sentences.zh: 寢夢日出室內，寤而見光自牖屬天，欻然有感。

translations.literal: She dreamed the sun rose within her chamber; waking, she saw light from the window reach the sky, and was suddenly moved.
translations.idiomatic: She dreamed the sun rose inside her lodge; waking, she saw light pour from the window to the sky and felt a sudden awe.

sentences.zh: 以建國三十四年七月七日生帝於參合陂北，其夜復有光明。

translations.literal: On the seventh day of the seventh month in the thirty-fourth year of Jianguo the Emperor was born north of Canhe Marsh, and that night there was light again.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventh day of the seventh month in Jianguo year thirty-four he was born north of Canhe Marsh, and light filled the night again.

sentences.zh: 昭成大悅，群臣稱慶，大赦，告於祖宗。

translations.literal: Zhaocheng was greatly pleased; the ministers offered congratulations, a general amnesty was proclaimed, and the ancestors were told.
translations.idiomatic: Zhaocheng rejoiced; ministers celebrated, the realm was pardoned, and the ancestors were notified.

sentences.zh: 保者以帝體重倍于常兒，竊獨奇怪。

translations.literal: The nurse found the infant twice the weight of ordinary children and marveled in private.
translations.idiomatic: His nurse found him twice the weight of other infants and marveled in secret.

sentences.zh: 明年有榆生於藏胞之坎，後遂成林。

translations.literal: The next year an elm sprang up in the hollow of the birth-curtain and later became a grove.
translations.idiomatic: Next year an elm grew in the hollow where the birth-curtain had stood and later became a wood.

sentences.zh: 帝弱而能言，目有光曜，廣顙大耳。

translations.literal: Though still young the Emperor could speak; his eyes shone with light, his brow was broad and his ears large.
translations.idiomatic: He spoke while still a child; his eyes shone, his brow was broad, his ears large.

sentences.zh: 六歲而昭成崩，苻堅遣將內侮，將遷帝長安，賴燕鳳乃免。

translations.literal: At six years Zhaocheng died; Fu Jian sent generals to invade within the borders, and they meant to move the Emperor to Chang'an, but thanks to Yan Feng he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: At six Zhaocheng died; Fu Jian sent generals south of the border intending to take the boy to Chang'an, but Yan Feng saved him.

sentences.zh: 堅軍既還，國眾離散。

translations.literal: Once Jian's army had withdrawn, the people of the state scattered.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian's army left, the nation fell apart.

sentences.zh: 堅使劉庫仁、劉衛辰分攝國事。

translations.literal: Jian sent Liu Kuren and Liu Weichen to divide control of state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jian set Liu Kuren and Liu Weichen to divide rule of the realm.

sentences.zh: 南部大人長孫嵩及元他等盡將故人眾南依庫仁，帝於是轉在獨孤部。

translations.literal: Southern chief Zhangsun Song and Yuan Ta and others led all their old followers south to join Kuren, and the Emperor thereupon passed into the Dugu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: Southern chief Zhangsun Song, Yuan Ta, and others took their old followers south to Kuren, and the boy passed into the Dugu tribe.

sentences.zh: 元年，葬昭成皇帝于金陵，營梓宮木柿盡生成林。

translations.literal: In the first year Zhaocheng Emperor was buried at Jinling; timbers for the outer coffin and inner chamber all grew into a forest where they were set.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year they buried Zhaocheng at Jinling; timbers for the tomb all sprouted and became a grove.

sentences.zh: 帝雖沖幼，而嶷然不群。

translations.literal: Though still a child, the Emperor stood apart from the crowd.
translations.idiomatic: Though still a boy, he stood apart from other children.

sentences.zh: 劉庫仁常謂其子曰：「帝有高天下之志，必興復洪業。」

translations.literal: Liu Kuren often told his sons, "This boy has the will to rule all under Heaven; he will surely restore the great enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Kuren often told his sons, "This child means to rule the world; he will restore the great enterprise."

sentences.zh: 七年十月，晉敗苻堅於淮南。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the seventh year Jin defeated Fu Jian at Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the seventh year Jin routed Fu Jian at Huainan.

sentences.zh: 慕容文等殺劉庫仁，弟眷代攝國部。

translations.literal: Murong Wen and others killed Liu Kuren, and his younger brother Juan took charge of the tribal division.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Wen and others killed Liu Kuren; his brother Juan took the tribe.

sentences.zh: 八年，慕容暐弟沖僭立。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Murong Wei's younger brother Chong usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Murong Wei's brother Chong seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 姚萇自稱大單于、萬年秦王。

translations.literal: Yao Chang styled himself Grand Chanyu and Everlasting King of Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang proclaimed himself Grand Chanyu and Everlasting King of Qin.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂僭稱燕王。

translations.literal: Murong Chui usurped the title King of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui seized the title King of Yan.

sentences.zh: 九年，劉庫仁子顯殺眷而代之，乃將謀逆。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Liu Kuren's son Xian killed Juan and replaced him, and then plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Liu Kuren's son Xian killed Juan, took his place, and plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 商人王霸知之，履帝足於眾中，帝乃馳還。

translations.literal: The merchant Wang Ba learned of it and trod on the Emperor's foot in the crowd; the Emperor thereupon galloped away.
translations.idiomatic: Merchant Wang Ba learned of the plot and stepped on the Emperor's foot in the crowd; the boy galloped away.

sentences.zh: 是時，故大人梁盆子六眷為顯謀主，盡知其計，密使部人穆崇馳告。

translations.literal: At that time the former great chief Liujuan of the Liang Penzi clan was Xian's chief plotter and knew the whole design; he secretly sent his tribesman Mu Chong in haste to report it.
translations.idiomatic: Former great chief Liujuan of Liang Penzi's line was Xian's chief plotter and knew the whole plan; he secretly sent Mu Chong to warn the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝乃陰結舊臣長孫犍、元他等，因幸賀蘭部。

translations.literal: The Emperor then secretly joined his old ministers Zhangsun Jian, Yuan Ta, and others, and on a tour of favor entered the Helan tribe.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly rallied old ministers Zhangsun Jian, Yuan Ta, and others and took refuge with the Helan tribe.

sentences.zh: 其日，顯果使人殺帝，不及。

translations.literal: That very day Xian indeed sent men to kill the Emperor, but they did not reach him in time.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Xian sent killers after the Emperor, but they arrived too late.

sentences.zh: 語在《獻明太后傳》。

translations.literal: The account is in the 《Biography of Empress Dowager Xianming》.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in the 《Biography of Empress Dowager Xianming》.

sentences.zh: 是歲，乞伏國仁私署秦、河二州牧、大單于。

translations.literal: That year Qifu Guoren privately assumed the offices of Governor of Qin and He provinces and Grand Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: That year Qifu Guoren privately took the titles Governor of Qin and He and Grand Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 姚萇殺苻堅，堅子丕僭即皇帝位於晉陽。

translations.literal: Yao Chang killed Fu Jian; Jian's son Pi usurped the imperial throne at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Chang killed Fu Jian; Jian's son Pi seized the throne at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 登國元年春正月戊申，帝即代王位，郊天建元，大會于牛川。

translations.literal: In the first month of the first year of Dengguo, on day wushen, the Emperor assumed the kingship of Dai, sacrificed to Heaven, established the reign era, and held a great assembly at Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of Dengguo year one, on wushen day in the first month, he became King of Dai, sacrificed to Heaven, proclaimed a reign era, and held court at Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 復以長孫嵩為南部大人，以叔孫普洛為北部大人。

translations.literal: In that month Zhangsun Song was again made southern chief and Shusun Puluo northern chief.
translations.idiomatic: That month Zhangsun Song was again southern chief and Shusun Puluo northern chief.

sentences.zh: 是月，慕容垂僭即皇帝位於中山，國號燕。

translations.literal: In that month Murong Chui usurped the imperial throne at Zhongshan, with the state name Yan.
translations.idiomatic: That month Murong Chui took the imperial title at Zhongshan and named his state Yan.

sentences.zh: 二月，幸定襄之盛樂，息眾課農。

translations.literal: In the second month he visited Shengle in Dingxiang and let the people rest while urging them to farm.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he went to Shengle in Dingxiang, gave the people rest, and urged them to farm.

sentences.zh: 慕容沖為其部下所殺。

translations.literal: Murong Chong was killed by his own subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chong was killed by his own men.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，改稱魏王。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer he changed his title to King of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he took the title King of Wei.

sentences.zh: 五月，姚萇僭即皇帝位於長安，國號大秦。

translations.literal: In the fifth month Yao Chang usurped the imperial throne at Chang'an, with the state name Great Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yao Chang seized the throne at Chang'an and named his state Great Qin.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，劉顯遣弟亢泥迎皇叔父窟咄于慕容永，以兵隨之，來逼南境。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn Liu Xian sent his younger brother Kangni to welcome his royal uncle Kudu from Murong Yong, and troops followed, pressing the southern border.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Liu Xian sent his brother Kangni to fetch his uncle Kudu from Murong Yong with an army that pressed the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 帝左右于桓等與諸部大人謀應之。

translations.literal: Yu Huan at the Emperor's side and the great chiefs of the tribes plotted to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Huan and the tribal chiefs at court plotted to go over to the enemy.

sentences.zh: 事泄，誅造謀者五人，餘悉不問。

translations.literal: The plot was discovered; five ringleaders were executed and the rest were not questioned.
translations.idiomatic: The plot leaked; five plotters were put to death and the rest went unpunished.

sentences.zh: 帝慮內難，乃北逾陰山，幸賀蘭部，阻山為固。

translations.literal: Fearing civil strife, the Emperor crossed Yinshan to the north and visited the Helan tribe, taking the mountains as his defense.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing civil war, he crossed Yinshan north to the Helan tribe and held the mountains as his fortress.

sentences.zh: 遣行人安同、長孫賀征師于慕容垂。

translations.literal: He sent the envoy An Tong and Zhangsun He to Murong Chui to ask for troops.
translations.idiomatic: He sent An Tong and Zhangsun He to Murong Chui to beg for troops.

sentences.zh: 垂令其子賀驎率師隨同等。

translations.literal: Chui ordered his son Helin to lead troops and follow Tong and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Chui sent his son Helin with an army to join Tong.

sentences.zh: 軍未至而寇逼。

translations.literal: The army had not yet arrived when the enemy pressed close.
translations.idiomatic: Before the army arrived, the enemy was upon him.

sentences.zh: 於是北部大人叔孫普洛等十三人及諸烏丸亡奔衛辰。

translations.literal: Thereupon northern chief Shusun Puluo and thirteen others, with various Wuhuan bands, fled to Liu Weichen.
translations.idiomatic: Northern chief Shusun Puluo and thirteen others, with Wuhuan bands, fled to Liu Weichen.

sentences.zh: 帝自弩山幸牛川，屯于延水，南出代谷，會賀驎于高柳，大破窟咄，悉收其眾。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself went from Nushan to Niuchuan, encamped on the Yan River, marched south through Daigu Valley, joined Helin at Gaoliu, routed Kudu utterly, and gathered in all his followers.
translations.idiomatic: He marched from Nushan to Niuchuan, camped on the Yan River, came south through Daigu Valley, met Helin at Gaoliu, shattered Kudu, and took all his people.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，苻丕為晉將馮該所殺。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter Fu Pi was killed by the Jin general Feng Gai.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Fu Pi was killed by Jin general Feng Gai.

sentences.zh: 慕容永僭即皇帝位於長子。

translations.literal: Murong Yong usurped the imperial throne at Changzi.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yong seized the throne at Changzi.

sentences.zh: 十一月，苻登僭即皇帝位於隴東。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Fu Deng usurped the imperial throne in Longdong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Fu Deng took the throne in Longdong.

sentences.zh: 十二月，慕容垂遣使奉帝西單于印綬，封上谷王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Murong Chui sent envoys bearing the seal of Western Chanyu and enfeoffed him as King of Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Murong Chui sent envoys with the Western Chanyu seal and made him King of Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The Emperor would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 二年夏五月，遣安同徵兵于慕容垂。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer in the second year he sent An Tong to levy troops from Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the second year he sent An Tong to Murong Chui for troops.

sentences.zh: 垂遣子賀驎率眾來會。

translations.literal: Chui sent his son Helin with a host to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Chui sent Helin with an army to join him.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝親征劉顯，顯奔慕容永，盡收其部落。

translations.literal: In the sixth month the Emperor campaigned in person against Liu Xian; Xian fled to Murong Yong and all his tribes were gathered in.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he marched in person against Liu Xian; Xian fled to Murong Yong and all his tribes were taken.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，巡松漠，還幸牛川。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter he toured Songmo and returned to Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he toured Songmo and returned to Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 三年夏五月癸亥，北征庫莫奚，大破之。

translations.literal: On day guihai in the fifth month of summer in the third year he marched north against the Kumo Xi and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day in the fifth month of the third year he marched north against the Kumo Xi and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 六月，乞伏國仁死，其弟乾歸立，私署河南王。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Qifu Guoren died; his younger brother Qiangui succeeded and privately assumed the title King of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Qifu Guoren died; his brother Qiangui took power and styled himself King of Henan.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，庫莫奚部帥鳩集遺散，夜犯行宮，縱騎撲討，盡滅之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the Kumo Xi chief Jiuji gathered the scattered and by night attacked the traveling palace; cavalry were sent in pursuit and they were wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Kumo Xi chief Jiuji rallied the scattered and struck the traveling palace by night; cavalry ran them down and destroyed them.

sentences.zh: 八月，使九原公儀于慕容垂。

translations.literal: In the eighth month he sent the Duke of Jiuyuan Yi on a mission to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he sent Duke of Jiuyuan Yi to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，垂遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter Chui sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Chui sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月甲寅，襲高車諸部落。

translations.literal: On day jiayin in the first month of spring in the fourth year he raided the Gaoche tribes.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day in the first month of the fourth year he raided the Gaoche tribes.

sentences.zh: 二月癸巳，遂至女水，討叱突鄰部。

translations.literal: On day guisi in the second month he reached Nüshui and attacked the Chituolin tribe.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day in the second month he reached Nüshui and attacked the Chituolin tribe.

sentences.zh: 並大破之。

translations.literal: Both were utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Both were shattered.

sentences.zh: 是月，呂光自稱三河王。

translations.literal: In that month Lü Guang styled himself King of the Three Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: That month Lü Guang took the title King of the Three Rivers.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，使陳留公虔于慕容垂。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer he sent the Duke of Chenliu Qian on a mission to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he sent Duke of Chenliu Qian to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，垂遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter Chui sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Chui sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五年春三月甲申，西征，次鹿渾海，襲高車袁紇部，大破之。

translations.literal: On day jiashen in the third month of spring in the fifth year he marched west, halted at Luhun Sea, and raided the Yuanhe band of the Gaoche, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day in the third month of the fifth year he marched west to Luhun Sea, struck the Yuanhe Gaoche, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂遣子賀驎來會。

translations.literal: Murong Chui sent his son Helin to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui sent Helin to join him.

sentences.zh: 夏四月丙寅，行幸意辛山，與賀驎討賀蘭、紇奚諸部落，大破之。

translations.literal: On day bingyin in the fourth month of summer he traveled to Yixin Mountain and with Helin attacked the Helan and Hexi tribes, routing them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day in the fourth month he went to Yixin Mountain and with Helin broke the Helan and Hexi tribes.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，還幸牛川。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn he returned to Niuchuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he returned to Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 使秦王觚于慕容垂。

translations.literal: He sent Prince Gu of Qin on a mission to Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Prince Gu of Qin to Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 九月壬申，討叱奴部囊曲水，破之。

translations.literal: On day renshen in the ninth month he attacked the Chinu tribe at Nangqu River and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen day in the ninth month he struck the Chinu tribe at Nangqu River and broke them.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，討高車豆陳部於狼山，破之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter he attacked the Douchén band of the Gaoche at Wolf Mountain and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he attacked the Gaoche Douchén band at Wolf Mountain and broke them.

sentences.zh: 十二月，帝還次白漠。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Emperor returned and halted at White Desert.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he returned and camped at White Desert.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月，幸紐垤川。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the sixth year he visited Niudie River.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year he went to Niudie River.

sentences.zh: 三月，遣九原公儀、陳留公虔等西討黜弗部，大破之。

translations.literal: In the third month he sent the Duke of Jiuyuan Yi, the Duke of Chenliu Qian, and others west to attack the Chufu tribe and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he sent Dukes Yi of Jiuyuan and Qian of Chenliu west against the Chufu tribe and crushed them.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，祭天。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer he sacrificed to Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he sacrificed to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 秋七月壬申，講武于牛川。

translations.literal: On day renshen in the seventh month he held a martial review at Niuchuan.
