translations.idiomatic: On renshen day in the seventh month he held a martial review at Niuchuan.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂止秦王觚而求名馬，帝絕之。

translations.literal: Murong Chui detained Prince Gu of Qin and demanded famous horses; the Emperor refused.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui held Prince Gu and demanded famous horses; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 乃遣使于慕容永，永使其大鴻臚慕容鈞奉表勸進尊號。

translations.literal: He then sent envoys to Murong Yong; Yong sent his Grand Herald Murong Jun with a memorial urging him to advance in title and honor.
translations.idiomatic: He sent envoys to Murong Yong; Yong sent Grand Herald Murong Jun with a memorial urging him to take the imperial title.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝襲五原，屠之，收其積穀。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the Emperor raided Wuyuan, slaughtered it, and gathered its stored grain.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he raided Wuyuan, put it to the sword, and seized its granaries.

sentences.zh: 還紐垤川，于棝陽塞北樹碑記功。

translations.literal: Returning to Niudie River, he set up a stele north of Ziyang Pass to record his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Niudie River, he raised a stele north of Ziyang Pass to record his deeds.

sentences.zh: 冬十月戊戌，北征蠕蠕，追破之于大磧南商山下。

translations.literal: On day wuxu in the tenth month of winter he marched north against the Rouran and pursued them to rout south of Great Desert at Shangshan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuxu day in the tenth month he marched north against the Rouran and ran them down south of the Great Desert at Shangshan.

sentences.zh: 十一月戊辰，還幸紐垤川。

translations.literal: On day wuchen in the eleventh month he returned to Niudie River.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day in the eleventh month he returned to Niudie River.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，衛辰遣子直力鞮寇南部。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, Weichen sent his son Zhilidi to raid the southern marches.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin day Weichen sent his son Zhilidi against the south.

sentences.zh: 壬午，帝大破之於鐵歧山南，衛辰父子奔遁。

translations.literal: On day renwu the Emperor routed them utterly south of Tieshan Mountain; Weichen and his sons fled in flight.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu day the Emperor shattered them south of Iron Mound Mountain and Weichen and his sons fled.

sentences.zh: 十二月，滅之，衛辰少子屈丐亡奔薛於部。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he destroyed them; Weichen's youngest son Qu Gou fled in exile to the Xueyu tribe.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he wiped them out; Qu Gou, Weichen's youngest son, fled to the Xueyu clan.

sentences.zh: 自河以南，諸部悉平。

translations.literal: South of the river, all the tribes were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Every tribe south of the river was brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 收衛辰子弟宗黨無少長五千餘人，盡殺之。

translations.literal: He seized more than five thousand of Weichen's sons, younger kin, and clan followers, young and old alike, and put them all to death.
translations.idiomatic: He took Weichen's sons, kin, and clansmen, more than five thousand in all, and slaughtered every one.

sentences.zh: 是歲，起河南宮。

translations.literal: That year he began the Henan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That year work began on the Henan Palace.

sentences.zh: 七年春正月，幸木根山，遂次黑鹽池，饗群臣，北之美水。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the seventh year he visited Mugen Mountain, then halted at Black Salt Pool, feasted the ministers, and went north to Meishui.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventh year he went to Mugen Mountain, camped at Black Salt Pool, feasted his ministers, and traveled north to Meishui.

sentences.zh: 三月，還幸河南宮。

translations.literal: In the third month he returned to the Henan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he returned to the Henan Palace.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，行幸漠南，仍築巡台。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn he traveled to the south of the desert and also built a touring terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he toured south of the desert and built a patrol terrace.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，慕容永遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter Murong Yong sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Murong Yong sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 八年春正月，南巡。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the eighth year he toured south.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year he toured south.

sentences.zh: 二月，幸羖羊原，赴白樓。

translations.literal: In the second month he visited Guyang Plain and went on to White Tower.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he went to Guyang Plain and then to White Tower.

sentences.zh: 夏六月，北巡。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of summer he toured north.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he toured north.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，臨幸新壇。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn he visited the new altar.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he visited the new altar.

sentences.zh: 先是衛辰子屈丐奔薛幹部，征之不送。

translations.literal: Earlier Weichen's son Qu Gou had fled to the Xuegan tribe; when the Emperor campaigned against them they did not surrender him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Qu Gou had fled to the Xuegan tribe, and when the Emperor demanded him they refused to hand him over.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝南征薛幹部，屠其城。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Emperor campaigned south against the Xuegan tribe and slaughtered their city.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he marched south against the Xuegan tribe and put their stronghold to the sword.

sentences.zh: 九月，還幸河南宮。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he returned to the Henan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he returned to the Henan Palace.

sentences.zh: 九年春三月，北巡。

translations.literal: In the third month of spring in the ninth year he toured north.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the ninth year he toured north.

sentences.zh: 使東平西元儀屯田于河北五原，至於棝陽塞外。

translations.literal: He ordered Yuan Yi, Duke of Dongping, to establish garrison farms in Wuyuan north of the river, reaching beyond Yusun Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yuan Yi, Duke of Dongping, to open garrison farms in Wuyuan north of the river as far as Yusun Pass.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，田於河東。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer he hunted fields east of the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he hunted the fields east of the river.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，還幸河南宮。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn he returned to the Henan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he returned to the Henan Palace.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，蠕蠕社侖等率部落西走。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter the Rouran chief Shelun and others led their tribes west in flight.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Shelun of the Rouran and others led their tribes west.

sentences.zh: 是歲，姚萇子興僭立，殺苻登。

translations.literal: That year Yao Xing, son of Yao Chang, usurped the throne and killed Fu Deng.
translations.idiomatic: That year Yao Xing, Yao Chang's son, seized the throne and killed Fu Deng.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂滅永。

translations.literal: Murong Chui destroyed Murong Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Chui destroyed Murong Yong.

sentences.zh: 十年秋七月，慕容垂遣其子寶來寇五原。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the tenth year Murong Chui sent his son Bao to raid Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the tenth year Murong Chui sent his son Bao against Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 八月，帝親兵于河南。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the Emperor personally took the field at Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the Emperor led the army in person at Henan.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛未，寶燒船夜遁。

translations.literal: On day xinwei in the tenth month of winter Bao burned his boats and fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day in the tenth month Bao burned his boats and fled in the night.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝進軍濟河。

translations.literal: On day jimao the Emperor advanced the army across the river.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day the Emperor crossed the river with his army.

sentences.zh: 乙酉夕，至參合陂。

translations.literal: On the evening of day yiyou he reached Canhe Marsh.
translations.idiomatic: At evening on yiyou day he reached Canhe Marsh.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，大破之，禽其王公以下文武將吏數千人。

translations.literal: On day bingxu he routed them utterly and captured several thousand princes, dukes, civil and military officers and generals.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu day he crushed them and took several thousand princes, dukes, and officers.

sentences.zh: 於俘虜中擢其才識者賈彝、賈閏、晁崇等參謀議，憲章故實。

translations.literal: From among the captives he selected men of talent and learning such as Jia Yi, Jia Run, and Chao Chong to take part in counsel and to restore statutes and precedent.
translations.idiomatic: From the prisoners he drew men of talent such as Jia Yi, Jia Run, and Chao Chong into counsel on laws and precedent.

sentences.zh: 十二月，還幸雲中之盛樂。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he returned to Shengle in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he returned to Shengle in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 皇始元年春正月，大蒐於定襄，因東幸善無北陂。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Huangshi he held a great hunt at Dingxiang and then traveled east to the northern slope at Shanwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Huangshi year one he held a great hunt at Dingxiang and went east to the northern slope at Shanwu.

sentences.zh: 三月，慕容垂寇桑乾川，陳留公虔死之。

translations.literal: In the third month Murong Chui raided Sanggan River and Duke Qian of Chenliu died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Murong Chui struck the Sanggan River and Duke Qian of Chenliu fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 垂遂至平城西北，聞帝將至，乃築城自守。

translations.literal: Chui then reached northwest of Pingcheng; hearing that the Emperor was coming, he built a walled camp to hold his ground.
translations.idiomatic: Chui pressed on to northwest of Pingcheng; when he heard the Emperor was near, he walled himself in.

sentences.zh: 疾甚，遂遁，死于上穀。

translations.literal: His illness grew grave and he fled; he died at Shanggu.
translations.idiomatic: His illness worsened and he fled; he died at Shanggu.

sentences.zh: 子寶秘喪，還至中山乃僭立。

translations.literal: His son Bao concealed the death and returned to Zhongshan before usurping the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Bao hid his father's death and returned to Zhongshan before seizing the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏六月丁亥，皇太后賀氏崩。

translations.literal: On day dinghai in the sixth month of summer the empress dowager, Lady He, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day in the sixth month Empress Dowager He died.

sentences.zh: 是月，葬獻明太后。

translations.literal: That month the Xianming Empress Dowager was buried.
translations.idiomatic: That month they buried the Xianming Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 呂光僭稱天王，國號涼。

translations.literal: Lü Guang usurped the title Heavenly King and named his state Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang took the title Heavenly King and founded the state of Liang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，左司馬許謙上書勸進尊號，於是改元，始建天子旌旗，出警入蹕。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Left Marshal of the Masters of Writing Xu Qian submitted a memorial urging him to advance in title and honor; thereupon he changed the reign era, first raised the imperial banners, and went forth and returned with imperial halts.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Xu Qian, Left Marshal of the Masters of Writing, urged him to take the imperial title; he changed the era name, raised the imperial standard, and began imperial progresses with halting attendants.

sentences.zh: 八月己亥，大舉討慕容寶。

translations.literal: On day jihai in the eighth month he launched a great campaign against Murong Bao.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai day in the eighth month he opened a great campaign against Murong Bao.

sentences.zh: 帝親勒六軍四十餘萬南出馬邑，逾句注，旌旗絡繹二千餘里，鼓行而前，人屋皆震。

translations.literal: The Emperor personally led more than four hundred thousand of the six armies south from Mayi, crossed Gouzhu Pass, and for more than two thousand li his banners and pennants stretched without end; they advanced to the beat of drums, and people and houses trembled.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor led more than four hundred thousand men south from Mayi, crossed Gouzhu Pass, and for two thousand li banners filled the road; drums drove the march, and the earth shook under foot.

sentences.zh: 別詔將軍封真等從東道襲幽州，圍薊。

translations.literal: A separate edict ordered General Feng Zhen and others to strike Youzhou by the eastern route and besiege Ji.
translations.idiomatic: By separate edict Feng Zhen and other generals struck Youzhou from the east and besieged Ji.

sentences.zh: 九月戊午，次陽曲，乘西山，臨觀晉陽。

translations.literal: On day wuwu in the ninth month he halted at Yangqu, ascended the western hills, and looked down on Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day in the ninth month he camped at Yangqu, climbed the western hills, and gazed on Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 寶并州牧、遼西王農棄城遁，并州平。

translations.literal: Bao's Governor of Bingzhou and Prince of Liaoxi, Nong, abandoned the city and fled; Bingzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Nong, Bao's governor of Bingzhou and Prince of Liaoxi, fled the city and Bingzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 初建台省，置百官，封拜公、侯、將軍、刺史、太守。

translations.literal: For the first time he established the court and ministries, set up the hundred offices, and enfeoffed dukes, marquises, generals, regional inspectors, and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: He founded the court and ministries for the first time, appointed the hundred offices, and enfeoffed dukes, marquises, generals, inspectors, and prefects.

sentences.zh: 尚書郎以下悉用文人。

translations.literal: From Masters of Writing clerks downward, all were men of letters.
translations.idiomatic: From clerks of the Masters of Writing down, every post went to literati.

sentences.zh: 帝初拓中原，留心慰納。

translations.literal: When the Emperor first opened the central plains, he gave his heart to comforting and winning men over.
translations.idiomatic: As he first pushed into the central plains, he devoted himself to winning people over.

sentences.zh: 諸士大夫詣軍門者，無少長皆引入，人得盡言，苟有微能，咸蒙敘用。

translations.literal: Scholars and officials who came to the army gate, whether young or old, he brought in without distinction; each might speak his fill, and if there was the slightest ability, all received appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars who came to his camp, young or old alike, were admitted to speak; anyone with the least talent was given office.

sentences.zh: 己未，詔輔國將軍奚牧略地晉川，獲慕容寶、丹楊王買得等於平陶城。

translations.literal: On day jiwei he ordered Supporting-the-State General Xi Mu to overrun Jinchuan and captured Murong Bao, Prince of Danyang Maidé, and others at Pingtao city.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day he ordered Xi Mu, Supporting-the-State General, to overrun Jinchuan and took Murong Bao, Prince of Danyang Maidé, and others at Pingtao.

sentences.zh: 九月，晉孝武帝殂。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Emperor Xiaowu of Jin died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Emperor Xiaowu of Jin died.

sentences.zh: 冬十一月庚子朔，帝至真定。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eleventh month of winter, day gengzi, the Emperor reached Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day, the new moon of the eleventh month, the Emperor reached Zhending.

sentences.zh: 自常山以東，守宰或捐城奔竄，或稽顙軍門，唯中山、鄴、信都三城不下。

translations.literal: East of Changshan, prefects and magistrates either abandoned their cities and fled or came to the army gate and bowed their foreheads to the ground; only Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu held out.
translations.idiomatic: East of Changshan, local rulers either fled their posts or came to prostrate at the camp gate; only Zhongshan, Ye, and Xindu still resisted.

sentences.zh: 別詔東平公儀攻鄴，冠軍將軍王建、左軍將軍李栗等攻信都，軍所行不得傷桑棗。

translations.literal: By separate edict Duke Yi of Dongping attacked Ye, Champion General Wang Jian, Left Army General Li Li, and others attacked Xindu, and the armies were forbidden to harm mulberry trees or jujubes.
translations.idiomatic: By separate edict Duke Yi of Dongping besieged Ye while Wang Jian the Champion General and Li Li the Left Army General besieged Xindu; the troops were forbidden to touch mulberry or jujube.

sentences.zh: 戊午，進軍中山。

translations.literal: On day wuwu he advanced the army to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day he marched on Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 己未，圍之。

translations.literal: On day jiwei he besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day he laid siege.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕量寶不能出戰，必憑城自守，急攻則傷士，久守則費糧，不如先平鄴、信都，然後還取中山。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I judge that Bao cannot give battle and is sure to rely on the walls and hold out. To press the assault will wound the soldiers; to hold a long siege will waste grain. Better first to pacify Ye and Xindu, then return and take Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Bao will not come out to fight; he will only cling to the walls. A hasty assault will cost men, a long siege will eat the grain. Let us take Ye and Xindu first, then come back for Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 」諸將稱善。

translations.literal: " The generals declared it good.
translations.idiomatic: The generals agreed.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，車駕幸魯口城。

translations.literal: On day dingmao the imperial carriage visited Lukou city.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao day the court moved to Lukou city.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月壬戌，帝引騎圍信都。

translations.literal: On day renxu in the first month of spring in the second year the Emperor led cavalry to besiege Xindu.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the first month of the second year the Emperor led cavalry to besiege Xindu.

sentences.zh: 其夜，寶冀州刺史、宜都王慕容鳳逾城奔中山。

translations.literal: That night Bao's Governor of Jizhou and Prince of Yidu, Murong Feng, climbed over the wall and fled to Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: That night Murong Feng, Bao's governor of Jizhou and Prince of Yidu, climbed the wall and fled to Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，寶輔國將軍張驤、護軍將軍徐超舉城降。

translations.literal: On day guihai Bao's Supporting-the-State General Zhang Yang and Protecting-the-Army General Xu Chao surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day Zhang Yang, Bao's Supporting-the-State General, and Xu Chao the Protecting-the-Army General surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 是月，鮮卑禿發烏孤私署大單于、西平王。

translations.literal: That month the Xianbei Tufa Wuji privately styled himself Grand Chanyu and King of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Xianbei chief Tufa Wuji took the titles Grand Chanyu and King of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 二月丁丑，帝軍于钜鹿之柏肆塢，臨滹沱水。

translations.literal: On day dingchou in the second month the Emperor encamped at Bozhi Hill in Julu, on the Hutuo River.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou day in the second month the Emperor camped at Bozhi Hill in Julu, on the Hutuo River.

sentences.zh: 其夜，寶悉眾犯營，燎及行宮，兵人駭散。

translations.literal: That night Bao mustered all his forces and struck the camp; fire reached the traveling palace and soldiers and men scattered in panic.
translations.idiomatic: That night Bao threw his whole army against the camp; flames reached the traveling palace and the troops broke in terror.

sentences.zh: 帝驚起，不及衣冠，跣出擊鼓。

translations.literal: The Emperor started up in alarm, had no time for robe or cap, and ran out barefoot to beat the drum.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor leapt up, seized neither robe nor cap, and ran out barefoot to beat the alarm drum.

sentences.zh: 俄而，左右及中軍將士稍集。

translations.literal: Before long the guards at hand and the central army officers and soldiers gradually gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his guards and the central army began to rally.

sentences.zh: 帝設奇陣，列烽營外，縱騎沖之。

translations.literal: The Emperor set an ambush formation, lined beacon fires outside the camp, and sent cavalry to charge them.
translations.idiomatic: He laid an ambush, set beacon fires beyond the camp, and sent cavalry to charge.

sentences.zh: 寶眾大敗，走還中山，獲其器械數十萬計。

translations.literal: Bao's host was utterly defeated and fled back to Zhongshan; weapons and gear captured were reckoned in the hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Bao's army was shattered and fled to Zhongshan; weapons taken numbered in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 寶尚書閔亮、秘書監崔逞等降者相屬，賜拜職爵各有差。

translations.literal: Bao's Masters of Writing Min Liang, Secretariat Director Cui Cheng, and others who surrendered came one after another and were granted offices and ranks each according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Min Liang of Bao's Masters of Writing, Cui Cheng the Secretariat Director, and others who surrendered were given offices and ranks according to merit.

sentences.zh: 三月己酉，車駕次盧奴。

translations.literal: On day jiyou in the third month the imperial carriage halted at Lunu.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou day in the third month the court camped at Lunu.

sentences.zh: 寶求和，請送秦王觚，割常山以西奉魏，乞守中山以東。

translations.literal: Bao sued for peace, asking to send Prince Gu of Qin, to cede the lands west of Changshan to Wei, and to hold Zhongshan east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Bao sued for peace, offering to send Prince Gu of Qin, cede everything west of Changshan to Wei, and keep only the lands east of the mountains around Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor consented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 已而寶背約。

translations.literal: Before long Bao broke the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bao broke his word.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，車駕次中山，命將圍之。

translations.literal: On day xinhai the imperial carriage halted at Zhongshan and ordered the generals to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day the court came to Zhongshan and ordered a siege.

sentences.zh: 是夜，寶弟賀驎將妻子走西山。

translations.literal: That night Bao's younger brother He Lin led his wife and children to flee to the western hills.
translations.idiomatic: That night Bao's brother He Lin fled west into the hills with his family.

sentences.zh: 寶恐賀驎先據和龍，壬子夜，北遁。

translations.literal: Bao feared that He Lin would seize Helong first; on the night of day renzi he fled north.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing He Lin would take Helong first, Bao fled north on the night of renzi day.

sentences.zh: 城內共立慕容普鄰為主。

translations.literal: Within the city they jointly set up Murong Pulin as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: The city set up Murong Pulin as their lord.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，帝以軍糧不繼，詔東平公儀罷鄴圍，徙屯巨鹿。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, because army grain could not keep up, he ordered Duke Yi of Dongping to lift the siege of Ye and move camp to Julu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month, with supplies failing, he ordered Duke Yi of Dongping to raise the siege of Ye and move to Julu.

sentences.zh: 五月庚子，帝以中山城內為普鄰所脅，乃招喻之。

translations.literal: On day gengzi in the fifth month, because those within Zhongshan were coerced by Pulin, he sent messages to win them over.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day in the fifth month, seeing the city held hostage by Pulin, he sent envoys to win the people over.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，曜兵揚威，以示城內，命諸軍罷圍南徙，以待其變。

translations.literal: On day jiachen he displayed his troops to show might before the city, ordered the armies to lift the siege and move south, and waited for the city to change.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day he paraded his army before the walls, drew off the siege southward, and waited for the city to turn.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，以東平公儀為左丞相，封衛王。

translations.literal: On day jiayin he made Duke Yi of Dongping Left Chancellor and enfeoffed him as Prince of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day he made Duke Yi of Dongping Left Chancellor and Prince of Wei.

sentences.zh: 進襄城公題爵為王。

translations.literal: He advanced Duke Ti of Xiangcheng to princely rank.
translations.idiomatic: He raised Duke Ti of Xiangcheng to prince.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，普鄰遣烏丸、張驤率五千餘人出城求食，寇靈壽。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Pulin sent the Wuhuan Zhang Yang with more than five thousand men out of the city to forage and raid Linghou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Pulin sent Zhang Yang the Wuhuan with five thousand men to forage and raid Linghou.

sentences.zh: 賀驎自丁零中入軍，因其眾，復入中山，殺普鄰而自立。

translations.literal: He Lin entered the army from among the Dingling, rallied their forces, re-entered Zhongshan, killed Pulin, and set himself up as ruler.
translations.idiomatic: He Lin came in from the Dingling tribes, gathered their men, re-entered Zhongshan, killed Pulin, and made himself ruler.

sentences.zh: 八月丙寅朔，帝進軍九門。

translations.literal: On the first day of the eighth month, day bingyin, the Emperor advanced the army to Jiumen.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day, the new moon of the eighth month, the Emperor marched on Jiumen.

sentences.zh: 時大疫，人馬牛死者十五六，中山猶拒守，群下咸思北還。

translations.literal: At that time a great pestilence raged; fifteen or sixteen of every hundred men, horses, and cattle died, yet Zhongshan still held out, and all below wished to return north.
translations.idiomatic: A great pestilence was abroad; men, horses, and cattle died by the tens of thousands, yet Zhongshan still held, and everyone below wanted to turn north.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，謂曰：「斯固天命，將若之何！

translations.literal: The Emperor knew it and said: "This is truly Heaven's decree; what can be done about it?
translations.idiomatic: Knowing their minds, the Emperor said, "This is Heaven's decree. What can we do?

sentences.zh: 四海之人皆可與為國，在吾所以撫之耳，何恤乎無人！

translations.literal: All the people within the four seas may be made into a state; it lies in how I comfort them. Why fear that there will be no men!
translations.idiomatic: Every man under heaven may be made a subject of the realm; it is only a matter of how I win them. Why fear there will be no people!

sentences.zh: 」群臣乃不敢言。

translations.literal: " The ministers then dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers dared not speak again.

sentences.zh: 九月，賀驎饑窮，率三萬餘人寇新市。

translations.literal: In the ninth month He Lin, hungry and desperate, led more than thirty thousand men to raid Xinyi.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month He Lin, starving and cornered, led more than thirty thousand men against Xinyi.

sentences.zh: 甲子晦，帝進軍討之。

translations.literal: On the last day of the month, day jiazi, the Emperor advanced the army to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day, the last day of the month, the Emperor marched out against him.

sentences.zh: 太史令晁崇奏曰：「不吉。

translations.literal: Grand Astrologer Chao Chong memorialized: "This is ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Astrologer Chao Chong said, "The day is ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「何也？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "How so?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "How so?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「紂以甲子亡，兵家忌之。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Zhou fell on a jiazi day; military men hold it in dread.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "King Zhou of Shang fell on a jiazi day; soldiers dread it.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「周武不以甲子勝乎？

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Did not King Wu of Zhou win on a jiazi day?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Did not King Wu of Zhou win on a jiazi day?

sentences.zh: 」崇無以對。

translations.literal: " Chong had no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had nothing to say.

sentences.zh: 冬十月丙寅，帝進軍新市，賀驎退阻泒水，依漸洳澤以自固。

translations.literal: On day bingyin in the tenth month of winter the Emperor advanced the army to Xinyi; He Lin retreated to block the Po River and relied on the Jianru Marsh to hold firm.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day in the tenth month the Emperor marched on Xinyi; He Lin fell back to the Po River and dug in among the marshes of Jianru.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，帝臨其營，戰於義台塢，大破之。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu the Emperor came to their camp and fought at Yitai Walled Hill; he routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day the Emperor faced their camp and fought at Eagle Terrace Hill; he crushed them.

sentences.zh: 賀驎單馬走鄴，慕容德殺之。

translations.literal: He Lin fled Ye on a single horse; Murong De killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He Lin fled alone on horseback toward Ye; Murong De killed him.

sentences.zh: 甲申，賀驎所署公卿尚書將吏士卒降者二萬餘人。

translations.literal: On day jiashen more than twenty thousand of the civil and military officers, Masters of Writing clerks, generals, and soldiers whom He Lin had appointed surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day more than twenty thousand officers and men whom He Lin had appointed surrendered.

sentences.zh: 其將張驤、李沈、慕容文等先來降，尋皆亡還，是日復獲之，皆赦而不問。

translations.literal: His generals Zhang Rang, Li Shen, Murong Wen, and others had come over first, then all fled back; that day they were captured again and all were pardoned without inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Generals Zhang Rang, Li Shen, and Murong Wen had surrendered earlier, then fled back; captured again that day, they were all pardoned.

sentences.zh: 獲其所傳皇帝璽綬、圖書、府庫珍寶。

translations.literal: They seized the imperial seal and cord of investiture he had passed down, books and documents, and the treasures of the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: They took the imperial seal and regalia, the archives, and the palace treasures.

sentences.zh: 中山平。

translations.literal: Zhongshan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan fell.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，襄城王題薨。

translations.literal: On day yiyou Prince Ti of Xiangcheng died.
translations.idiomatic: On yiyou day Prince Ti of Xiangcheng died.

sentences.zh: 天興元年春正月，慕容德走保滑台，衛王儀克鄴。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the first year of Tianxing, Murong De fled to hold Hua Terrace; Prince Yi of Wei took Ye.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianxing year one, Murong De withdrew to Hua Terrace; Prince Yi of Wei took Ye.

sentences.zh: 庚子，行幸真定，遂幸鄴。

translations.literal: On day gengzi he traveled to Zhending and then to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day he went to Zhending and then to Ye.

sentences.zh: 百姓有老病不能自存者，詔郡縣振恤之。

translations.literal: For commoners old or ill who could not support themselves, an edict ordered the commanderies and counties to relieve and sustain them.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered every commandery and county to care for the aged and sick among the people who could not support themselves.

sentences.zh: 帝至鄴，巡登臺榭，遍覽宮城，將有定都之志，乃置行台。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Ye he toured the terraces and towers, viewing the entire palace compound; he formed the intention to fix the capital there and set up a traveling secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At Ye he climbed the terraces and walked the palace grounds until he wished to make the city his capital; he established a traveling secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遂還中山，所過存問百姓。

translations.literal: He then returned to Zhongshan, inquiring after the people along the way.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to Zhongshan and inquired after the people in every place he passed.

sentences.zh: 詔大軍所經州郡皆復貲租一年，除山東人租賦之半。

translations.literal: An edict restored one year's tax burden in every commandery the great army had crossed, and halved the rent and levies of the people east of the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: An edict remitted one year's taxes in every commandery the army had crossed and cut the rent and levies of Shandong in half.

sentences.zh: 車駕將北還，發卒萬人通直道，自望都鐵關鑿恆嶺至代五百餘里。

translations.literal: As the imperial carriage prepared to return north, ten thousand laborers were levied to open a straight road, more than five hundred li from Wangdu through the Iron Pass of Mount Heng, cutting through the Heng Range to Dai.
translations.idiomatic: As the court prepared to go north, ten thousand men opened a straight road more than five hundred li from Wangdu through Iron Pass in the Heng Mountains to Dai.

sentences.zh: 帝慮還後山東有變，乃於中山置行台，詔衛王儀鎮之，使略陽公遵鎮勃海之合口。

translations.literal: The Emperor feared trouble in Shandong after his departure; therefore at Zhongshan he set up a traveling secretariat, ordering Prince Yi of Wei to hold it and Duke Zun of Liaoyang to hold the mouth of the Bohai at He Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing unrest in Shandong after he left, he set up a traveling secretariat at Zhongshan, left Prince Yi of Wei to guard it, and sent Duke Zun of Liaoyang to hold He Pass on the Bohai coast.

sentences.zh: 右軍將軍尹國先督租于冀州，聞帝將還，謀反，欲襲信都，安南將軍長孫嵩執送，斬之。

translations.literal: General of the Right Army Yin Guo had earlier overseen tax collection in Jizhou; hearing the Emperor would return, he plotted rebellion, intending to strike Xindu; Anping General Sun Ci seized and sent him forward and he was beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Guo the General of the Right had been collecting taxes in Jizhou; learning the Emperor was returning, he plotted to strike Xindu; Sun Ci the Anping General seized him and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，車駕發中山，至於望都堯山。

translations.literal: On day xinyou the imperial carriage set out from Zhongshan and reached Yaoshan at Wangdu.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day the court left Zhongshan and came to Yaoshan at Wangdu.

sentences.zh: 徙山東六州人吏及徒何、高麗雜夷、三十六署百工伎巧十餘萬口以充京師。

translations.literal: More than a hundred thousand households of officials and clerks from the six commanderies east of the mountains, together with Tuohe, Koguryo, and other mixed barbarians and craftsmen of the thirty-six offices, were moved to fill the capital.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred thousand people—officials from the six eastern commanderies, Tuohe and Koguryo and other tribes, and craftsmen from the thirty-six workshops—were moved to the capital.

sentences.zh: 車駕次於恆山之陽。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage halted south of Mount Heng.
translations.idiomatic: The court camped on the southern face of Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 博陵、勃海、章武諸郡群盜並起，略陽公遵等討之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose together in Boling, Bohai, Zhangwu, and other commanderies; Duke Zun of Liaoyang and others campaigned against them.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits rose in Boling, Bohai, Zhangwu, and other commanderies; Duke Zun of Liaoyang and others suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 是月，慕容德自稱燕王，據廣固。

translations.literal: That month Murong De styled himself King of Yan and held Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: That month Murong De declared himself King of Yan and took Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 二月，車駕至自中山。

translations.literal: In the second month the imperial carriage returned from Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month the court returned from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 幸繁畤宮。

translations.literal: He visited Fancan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He visited Fancan Palace.

sentences.zh: 更選屯衛。

translations.literal: The garrison guards were chosen anew.
translations.idiomatic: The palace guards were reorganized.

sentences.zh: 詔給內徙新戶耕牛，計口受田。

translations.literal: An edict granted plow oxen to newly resettled households and allotted fields by head count.
translations.idiomatic: An edict gave plow oxen to the newly resettled and allotted fields by the head.

sentences.zh: 三月，征左丞相、衛王儀還京師，詔略陽公遵代鎮中山。

translations.literal: In the third month he recalled Left Chancellor Prince Yi of Wei to the capital and ordered Duke Zun of Liaoyang to replace him as garrison commander at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he summoned Prince Yi of Wei, Left Chancellor, to the capital and sent Duke Zun of Liaoyang to replace him at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 夏四月壬戌，以曆陽公穆崇為太尉，钜鹿公長孫嵩為司徒，進封略陽公遵為常山王，南安公順為毗陵王。

translations.literal: On day renxu in the fourth month of summer he made Duke Chong of Liyang Grand Marshal, Duke Song of Julu Minister of State, advanced Duke Zun of Liaoyang to Prince of Changshan, and Duke Shun of Nan'an to Prince of Piling.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the fourth month he made Duke Chong of Liyang Grand Marshal, Duke Song of Julu Minister of State, raised Duke Zun of Liaoyang to Prince of Changshan, and Duke Shun of Nan'an to Prince of Piling.

sentences.zh: 祭天於西郊，旗幟有加焉。

translations.literal: He sacrificed to Heaven at the western suburb; his banners and pennants were augmented.
translations.idiomatic: He sacrificed to Heaven at the western suburb with heightened ceremony.

sentences.zh: 廣平太守、遼西公意列謀反，與郡人韓奇矯假讖圖，將襲鄴城。

translations.literal: Yilie, Duke of Liaoxi and Governor of Guangping, plotted rebellion with his fellow townsman Han Qi, forging prophetic charts, intending to strike Ye city.
translations.idiomatic: Yilie Duke of Liaoxi, governor of Guangping, conspired with Han Qi of his commandery to forge portents and seize Ye.

sentences.zh: 詔反者就郡賜死。

translations.literal: By edict the rebels were granted death in their own commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the rebels executed in their own commanderies.

sentences.zh: 是月，蘭汗殺慕容寶而自立為大單于、昌黎王。

translations.literal: That month Lan Han killed Murong Bao and set himself up as Grand Chanyu and King of Changli.
translations.idiomatic: That month Lan Han killed Murong Bao and made himself Grand Chanyu and King of Changli.

sentences.zh: 六月丙子，詔有司議定國號。

translations.literal: On day bingzi in the sixth month an edict ordered the officials to deliberate and fix the name of the state.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi day in the sixth month an edict ordered the officials to choose a name for the realm.

sentences.zh: 群臣奏曰：「昔周、秦以前，帝王居所生之土，及王天下，即承為號。

translations.literal: The ministers submitted: "In antiquity, before the Zhou and Qin, when emperors and kings dwelt in the land where they were born and then ruled all under Heaven, they took that land as their title."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers wrote, "Before Zhou and Qin, kings took the land of their birth as their dynastic name."

sentences.zh: 今國家啟基雲、代，應以代為號。

translations.literal: "Now the state was founded in Yun and Dai; they should take Dai as the name."
translations.idiomatic: Our realm rose in Yun and Dai; we should be called Dai.

sentences.zh: 」詔曰：「昔朕遠祖總禦幽都，控制遐國，雖踐王位，未定九州。

translations.literal: An edict said: "In antiquity Our remote ancestor held sway over the Dark North and controlled distant states; though he trod the royal throne, he did not fix the Nine Provinces."
translations.idiomatic: The edict answered, "Our remote ancestors ruled the north and held distant peoples in awe, yet even on the throne they did not unite the nine provinces."

sentences.zh: 逮于朕躬，掃平中土，凶逆蕩除，遐邇率服，宜仍先號為魏。

translations.literal: "As for Our person, We swept the central lands, swept away the wicked, and far and near submitted; We should still take the former title Wei."
translations.idiomatic: In his own time he had cleared the central plains and put down rebellion until all lands submit; the name should remain Wei.

sentences.zh: 」秋七月，遷都平城，始營宮室，建宗廟，立社稷。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the capital was moved to Pingcheng; palace halls were first built, the ancestral temple established, and the altar of soil and grain set up.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the capital moved to Pingcheng; work began on the palace, ancestral temple, and altars of state.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶子盛殺蘭汗而自立為長樂王。

translations.literal: Murong Bao's son Sheng killed Lan Han and set himself up as King of Changle.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng, son of Murong Bao, killed Lan Han and made himself King of Changle.

sentences.zh: 八月，詔有司正封畿，制郊甸，端徑術，標道里，平五權，較五量，定五度。

translations.literal: In the eighth month an edict ordered the officials to rectify the royal domain, define the suburban fields and hunting preserves, set straight roads and measures, mark the leagues, balance the five weights, check the five measures, and fix the five standards of length.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month an edict ordered officials to survey the royal demesne, define the suburbs, straighten roads and measures, and standardize weights, capacities, and units of length.

sentences.zh: 遣使循行郡國，舉奏守宰不法者，親覽察黜陟之。

translations.literal: Envoys were sent to tour the commanderies and kingdoms, reporting unlawful local administrators; the Emperor himself reviewed them for dismissal or promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys toured every commandery and kingdom, reporting corrupt governors; the Emperor read each case and promoted or removed men himself.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，起天文殿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter work began on the Hall of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month work began on the Astronomy Hall.

sentences.zh: 十一月辛亥，尚書吏部郎中鄧彥海典官制，立爵品，定律呂，協音樂。

translations.literal: On day xinhai Deng Yanhai, Director of the Bureau of Personnel in the Masters of Writing, oversaw the office regulations, established ranks of nobility, fixed pitch pipes, and harmonized music.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day Deng Yanhai of the Masters of Writing oversaw offices and ranks, fixed pitch pipes, and set the music in order.

sentences.zh: 儀曹郎中董謐撰郊廟、社稷、朝覲、饗宴之儀。

translations.literal: Dong Mi, Director of the Bureau of Rites, composed the rites for suburban sacrifice, ancestral temple, altar of soil and grain, court audience, and feast.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Mi of the Rites Bureau drafted the rites for sacrifice, temple worship, court audiences, and feasts.

sentences.zh: 三公郎中王德定律令，申科禁。

translations.literal: Wang De, Director of the Bureau of the Three Excellencies, shaped statutes and clarified prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: Wang De of the Three Excellencies Bureau drafted laws and clarified punishments.

sentences.zh: 太史令晁崇造渾儀，考天象。

translations.literal: Astronomer-royal Chao Chong made the armillary sphere and examined the heavens.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomer Royal Chao Chong built an armillary sphere and charted the heavens.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書崔宏總裁之。

translations.literal: Minister of the Masters of Writing Cui Hong had general oversight.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of the Masters of Writing Cui Hong supervised the whole undertaking.

sentences.zh: 閏月，左丞相衛王儀及王公卿士，詣闕上書曰：「臣等聞宸極居中，則列宿齊其晷。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month Left Chancellor Prince Yi of Wei together with princes, dukes, and ministers came to the palace gate with a memorial saying: "We have heard that when the polar lodestone is centered, the stars align their shadows."
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary month Prince Yi of Wei, Left Chancellor, with the princes, dukes, and ministers submitted a memorial: "When the pole stands at the center, every star wheels in its season."

sentences.zh: 帝王順天，則群後仰其度。

translations.literal: "When an emperor follows Heaven, the host of lords look up to his measure."
translations.idiomatic: When a sage king follows Heaven, every lord takes his measure from him.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下德協二儀，道隆三五，仁風被于四海，盛化塞于天區，澤及昆蟲，恩沾行葦，謳歌所屬，八表歸心。

translations.literal: "We consider that Your Majesty's virtue matches the Two Modes and your Way surpasses the Three and Five sovereigns; humane wind covers the four seas, flourishing transformation fills the heavenly regions, bounty reaches insects, grace moistens the running grass—where song and praise turn, the eight directions return their hearts."
translations.idiomatic: Your virtue matches heaven and earth and your Way outshines the sage kings of old; your mercy fills the seas, your transforming grace reaches insects and grass, and the eight directions turn to you in song.

sentences.zh: 而躬履謙虛，退身後己，宸儀未彰，袞服未禦，非所以上允皇天之意，下副樂推之心。

translations.literal: "Yet you remain humble, putting yourself after others; imperial rites are not displayed, full regalia is not worn—this is not what satisfies Heaven above or the people's urge to acclaim you."
translations.idiomatic: Yet you still hold yourself low and keep the imperial rites hidden; this cannot satisfy Heaven or the people's longing to acclaim you.

sentences.zh: 臣等謹昧死以聞。

translations.literal: "We humbly risk death to speak."
translations.idiomatic: We venture our lives to say so.

sentences.zh: 」帝三讓乃許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor thrice declined and then assented.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor refused three times, then consented.

sentences.zh: 十二月己丑，帝臨天文殿。

translations.literal: On day jichou in the twelfth month the Emperor took his seat in the Hall of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou day in the twelfth month the Emperor ascended the Astronomy Hall.

sentences.zh: 太尉、司徒進璽綬，百官咸稱萬歲。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal and Minister of State presented the seal and cord; the hundred officials all cried ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal and Minister of State presented the imperial seal; the officials shouted ten thousand years.

sentences.zh: 大赦，改元，追尊成帝以下及後號諡，樂用《皇始之舞 》。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed, the reign era was changed, posthumous titles were granted to former emperors and empresses, and the dance called The Emperor's Beginning was adopted for court music.
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed a general amnesty, changed the era name, gave posthumous titles to his forebears, and adopted the dance Beginning of the Sovereign for court music.

sentences.zh: 詔百司議定行次，尚書崔宏等奏從土德，服色尚黃，數用五，祖以未，臘以辰，犧牲用白，五郊立氣，宣贊時令，敬授人時，行夏之正。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the hundred offices to deliberate the dynastic element; Cui Hong and others of the Masters of Writing submitted that they should follow the power of Earth, honor yellow in dress, use five as the sacred number, take the Branch wei as dynastic ancestor and chen for the great winter sacrifice, use white victims, establish the qi of the five suburbs, proclaim the seasons, respectfully grant the seasons to men, and follow the Xia calendar.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered deliberation on the dynastic element; Cui Hong and others argued for the power of Earth, yellow vestments, the number five, white victims, rites at the five suburbs, and the Xia calendar.

sentences.zh: 徙六州二十二郡守宰豪傑吏人二千家於代都。

translations.literal: Two thousand households of powerful families, officials, and clerks from twenty-two commanderies of the six provinces were moved to the capital at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Two thousand leading households of officials and gentry from twenty-two commanderies in six provinces were moved to the capital.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月甲子，初祀上帝於南郊，以始祖神元皇帝配，降壇視燎，成禮而反。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the second year, on day jiazi, he first sacrificed to Shangdi at the southern suburb, with the Ancestor Emperor Shenyuan as associate; descending the altar he viewed the burning and returned when the rites were complete.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day in the first month of year two he sacrificed to Heaven at the southern suburb with Emperor Shenyuan as spirit partner, watched the flame from below the altar, and returned when the rite was done.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，赦京師。

translations.literal: On day yichou he pardoned the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou day he pardoned the capital.

sentences.zh: 始制三駕之法。

translations.literal: The law of the three imperial carriages was first established.
translations.idiomatic: He first established the rule of the three imperial progresses.

sentences.zh: 庚午，北巡。

translations.literal: On day gengwu he toured north.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day he toured north.

sentences.zh: 分命諸將大襲高車，常山王遵三軍從東道出長川，高涼王樂真等七軍從西道出牛川，車駕親勒六軍從中道自駮髯水西北出。

translations.literal: Separate orders sent the generals on a great strike against the Gaoche; Prince Zun of Changshan with three armies went out by the eastern road from Changchuan; Prince Yuezhen of Gaoliang and seven armies went out by the western road from Niuchuan; the Emperor personally led the six armies from the central road northwest from Boxu Water.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his generals against the Gaoche clans: Prince Zun of Changshan led three armies east from Changchuan, Prince Yuezhen of Gaoliang led seven armies west from Niuchuan, and the Emperor led six armies from the center northwest from Boxu River.

sentences.zh: 二月丁亥朔，諸軍同會，破高車雜種三十餘部。

translations.literal: On the first day of the second month, day dinghai, the armies united and broke more than thirty Gaoche tribes.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day, the new moon of the second month, the armies met and shattered more than thirty Gaoche tribes.

sentences.zh: 衛王儀督三將別從西北絕漠千餘里，破其遺迸七部。

translations.literal: Prince Yi of Wei led three generals separately from the northwest more than a thousand li across the desert and broke seven remnant tribes.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Wei led three generals more than a thousand li across the desert northwest and broke seven fleeing tribes.

sentences.zh: 還次牛川，及薄山，並刻石紀功。

translations.literal: Returning he halted at Niuchuan and Boshan, and at both carved stone to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: On the return he camped at Niuchuan and Thin Mountain and carved the victory in stone at both places.

sentences.zh: 以所獲高車眾起鹿苑于南台陰，北距長城，東苞白登，屬之西山，廣輪數十里，鑿渠引武川水，注之苑中，疏為三溝，分流宮城內外。

translations.literal: Using captives from the Gaoche he raised a deer park on the south face of South Terrace; north to the Long Wall, east embracing White Ascent, running to Western Mountain—tens of li in breadth; channels were cut to draw Wuchuan water into the park, opened into three canals dividing inside and outside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: With Gaoche captives he built a deer park south of South Terrace, running from the Long Wall north to White Ascent east and the western hills, tens of li across; canals brought Wuchuan River into the park in three channels threading through and around the palace.

sentences.zh: 又穿鴻雁池。

translations.literal: The Wild Goose Pool was also dug.
translations.idiomatic: He also dug the Wild Goose Pool.

sentences.zh: 三月己未，車駕至自北伐。

translations.literal: On day jiwei in the third month the imperial carriage returned from the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day in the third month the court returned from the northern expedition.

sentences.zh: 甲子，初令《五經》群書各置博士，增國子太學生員三千人。

translations.literal: On day jiazi he first ordered erudites for each of the Five Classics and group of books, adding three thousand students to the Imperial College.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day he appointed erudites for the Five Classics and other texts and added three thousand students to the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 是月，氐人李辯叛慕容德，求援於鄴。

translations.literal: That month the Di man Li Bian rebelled against Murong De and sought aid from Ye.
translations.idiomatic: That month Li Bian of the Di rebelled against Murong De and asked Ye for help.

sentences.zh: 行台尚書和跋以輕騎應之，克滑台，收德宮人府藏。

translations.literal: He Ba of the traveling Masters of Writing answered with light cavalry, took Hua Terrace, and seized De's palace women and treasury stores.
translations.idiomatic: He Ba of the traveling secretariat rode out with light cavalry, took Hua Terrace, and seized Murong De's women and stores.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，起天華殿。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn work began on the Celestial Splendor Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month work began on the Celestial Splendor Hall.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，大閱于鹿苑。

translations.literal: On day xinyou a great review was held at the deer park.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou day he held a great review at the deer park.

sentences.zh: 八月，增啟京城十二門，作西武庫。

translations.literal: In the eighth month the twelve gates of the capital were enlarged and the Western Armory built.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the capital's twelve gates were enlarged and the Western Armory was built.

sentences.zh: 除州郡人租賦之半。

translations.literal: Half the rent and levies of every commandery and prefecture were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Rent and levies were halved in every commandery and county.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，詔禮官備撰眾儀，著於新令。

translations.literal: On day xinhai an edict ordered the ritual officers to compile the full corpus of ceremonies and write them into the new statutes.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day an edict ordered ritual officers to compile all ceremonies for the new code.

sentences.zh: 范陽人盧溥聚眾海濱，稱幽州刺史，攻掠郡縣，殺幽州刺史封遝幹。

translations.literal: Lu Pu of Fanyang gathered a multitude on the seacoast, styled himself Inspector of You Province, attacked and raided commanderies and counties, and killed Feng Qigan, Inspector of You.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Pu of Fanyang raised a host on the coast, called himself Inspector of Youzhou, raided the commanderies, and killed Feng Qigan the inspector.

sentences.zh: 是月，禿發烏孤死，其弟利鹿孤立，遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That month Tufa Wuji died; his brother Lilugu succeeded and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That month Tufa Wuji died; his brother Lilugu succeeded him and sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，太廟成，遷神元、平文、昭成、獻明皇帝神主于太廟。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter the Grand Temple was completed; the spirit tablets of Emperors Shenyuan, Pingwen, Zhaocheng, and Xianming were moved to the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Grand Temple was finished and the tablets of Emperors Shenyuan, Pingwen, Zhaocheng, and Xianming were moved there.

sentences.zh: 十二月，天華殿成。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the Celestial Splendor Hall was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the Celestial Splendor Hall was finished.

sentences.zh: 呂光立其子紹為天王，自稱太上皇，及死，庶子纂殺紹而僭立。

translations.literal: Lü Guang installed his son Shao as Heavenly King, styled himself Exalted Emperor, and when he died his bastard son Zuan killed Shao and usurped the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Guang made his son Shao Heavenly King and took the title Exalted Emperor; when he died his bastard son Zuan killed Shao and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月戊午，材官將軍和突破盧溥於遼西，獲之，及其子煥傳送京師，轘之。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year, on day wuwu, Material Officers General He Po broke Lu Pu in Liaoxi, captured him and his son Huan, and sent them to the capital in bonds; they were torn apart by chariots.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day in the first month of year three General He Po defeated Lu Pu in Liaoxi, captured him and his son Huan, sent them to the capital, and had them torn apart by chariots.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，祀北郊。

translations.literal: On day guihai he sacrificed at the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai day he sacrificed at the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 分命諸官循行州郡，觀風俗，察舉不法。

translations.literal: Separate orders sent each office to tour the commanderies and kingdoms, observe customs, investigate and report lawlessness.
translations.idiomatic: He sent officers to tour the commanderies, observe local custom, and report corruption.

sentences.zh: 二月丁亥，詔有司祀日於東郊。

translations.literal: On day dinghai an edict ordered the officials to sacrifice to the sun at the eastern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day an edict ordered sacrifice to the sun at the eastern suburb.

sentences.zh: 始耕籍田。

translations.literal: The sacred field was first plowed.
translations.idiomatic: He first plowed the sacred field.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，皇子聰薨。

translations.literal: On day renyin Prince Cong died.
translations.idiomatic: On renyin day Prince Cong died.

sentences.zh: 三月戊午，立皇后慕容氏。

translations.literal: On day wuwu in the third month Empress Murong was installed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu day in the third month he installed Empress Murong.

sentences.zh: 是月，穿城南渠通於城內，作東西魚池。

translations.literal: That month the southern canal within the walls was dug through to the city and eastern and western fish ponds were made.
translations.idiomatic: That month a canal was cut south of the wall into the city and eastern and western fish ponds were dug.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，姚興遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer Yao Xing sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month Yao Xing sent envoys with tribute.

sentences.zh: 五月戊辰，詔謁者僕射張濟使於興。

translations.literal: On day wuchen an edict ordered Chief of Protocol Zhang Ji as envoy to Xing.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day he sent Zhang Ji Chief of Protocol as envoy to Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 己巳，東巡，遂幸涿鹿，遣使者乙太牢祀帝堯、帝舜廟。

translations.literal: On day jisi he toured east, then visited Zhuolu, and sent envoys to offer the great slaughter at the temples of Emperors Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi day he toured east to Zhuolu and sent envoys to offer the highest sacrifice at the temples of Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 西幸馬邑，觀氵壘源。

translations.literal: He traveled west to Mayi and viewed the Lei source.
translations.idiomatic: He went west to Mayi and viewed the Lei River source.

sentences.zh: 六月庚辰朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the sixth month, day gengchen, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen day, the new moon of the sixth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，乞伏乾歸大為姚興所破。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Qifu Gangui suffered a great defeat at the hands of Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Qifu Gangui was shattered by Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 壬子，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On day renzi the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi day the court returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 起中天殿及雲母堂、金華室。

translations.literal: The Central Heaven Hall and the Mica Hall, Golden Splendor Chamber, were raised.
translations.idiomatic: Work began on the Central Heaven Hall, the Mica Hall, and the Golden Splendor Chamber.

sentences.zh: 時太史屢奏天文錯亂，帝親覽經占，多雲宜改王易政，於是數革官號，欲以防塞凶狡，消弭災變。

translations.literal: The astronomers repeatedly reported heavenly disorder; the Emperor personally examined the classics of prognostication and many said the king should change title and transform government; therefore he repeatedly altered office names, wishing to block the cunning and wicked and dispel calamitous change.
translations.idiomatic: The astronomers kept reporting strange heavens; the Emperor studied the omen books himself, and since many said he should change his title and government, he altered office names again and again to ward off disaster.

sentences.zh: 已而慮臣下疑惑，冬十二月丙申，下詔述成敗之理，鑒殷、周之失，革秦、漢之弊，以喻臣下。

translations.literal: Yet he feared his ministers would be confused; on day bingchen in the twelfth month of winter he issued an edict setting forth the logic of success and failure, taking Yin and Zhou as mirrors for failure and Qin and Han as mirrors for abuses, to instruct his ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing confusion among his ministers, on bingchen day in the twelfth month he issued an edict on success and failure, taking Yin-Zhou and Qin-Han as lessons, to guide his officials.

sentences.zh: 是歲，河右諸郡奉、涼武昭王李玄盛為秦涼二州牧、涼公，肇興霸業，年號庚子。

translations.literal: That year the commanderies west of the Yellow River set up Li Xuansheng of Liang as Military Governor of Qin and Liang and Duke of Liang, founding a hegemony with the era name Gengzi.
translations.idiomatic: That year the northwestern commanderies made Li Xuansheng Duke of Liang and governor of Qin and Liang, beginning his rule with the era name Gengzi.

sentences.zh: 四年春二月丁亥，命樂師入學習舞，釋菜於先聖、先師。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the fourth year, on day dinghai, he ordered the music masters to enter the school to learn the dances and performed the vegetable-offering rite before the Former Sage and Former Teacher.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai day in the second month of the fourth year he had the court musicians train in the ritual dances and offered the school sacrifice to Confucius and his disciples.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，分命使者巡行州郡，聽察辭訟，糾劾不法。

translations.literal: On day dingyou separate orders sent envoys to tour the provinces and commanderies, hear lawsuits, and impeach the unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou day he sent envoys throughout the provinces to hear cases and punish corruption.

sentences.zh: 是月，呂光弟子隆弑呂纂而自立。

translations.literal: That month Lü Guang's nephew Long murdered Lü Zuan and set himself up in power.
translations.idiomatic: That month Long, nephew of Lü Guang, killed Lü Zuan and seized the throne.

sentences.zh: 三月，帝親漁，薦於寢廟。

translations.literal: In the third month the Emperor fished in person and presented the catch at the sleeping temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the Emperor fished himself and offered the catch at the ancestral sleeping hall.

sentences.zh: 夏四月辛卯，罷鄴行台。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on day xinmao, the traveling secretariat at Ye was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao day in the fourth month he abolished the traveling secretariat at Ye.

sentences.zh: 詔有司明揚隱逸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the officials to make manifest and promote recluses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered officials to seek out and recommend hidden worthies.

sentences.zh: 五月，起紫極殿、玄武樓、涼風觀、石池、鹿苑台。

translations.literal: In the fifth month work began on the Purple Pole Hall, Black Tortoise Tower, Cool Breeze View, Stone Pool, and Deer Park Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he began the Purple Pole Hall, Black Tortoise Tower, Cool Breeze Pavilion, Stone Pool, and Deer Park Terrace.

sentences.zh: 六月，盧水胡沮渠蒙遜私署涼州牧、張掖公。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Juqu Mengxun of the Lushui Hu privately styled himself Governor of Liang Province and Duke of Zhangye.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Juqu Mengxun of the Lushui Hu took the titles Governor of Liangzhou and Duke of Zhangye on his own authority.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，詔兗州刺史長孫肥南徇許昌、彭城。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn an edict ordered Yan Province Inspector Changsun Fei to campaign south against Xuchang and Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he ordered Changsun Fei, inspector of Yanzhou, to strike south at Xuchang and Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 詔賜天下鎮戍將士布帛各有差。

translations.literal: An edict granted cloth and silk to garrison soldiers throughout the realm in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: An edict gave graded gifts of cloth and silk to every garrison soldier in the realm.

sentences.zh: 八月，段興殺慕容盛，叔父熙盡誅段氏，僭即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the eighth month Duan Xing killed Murong Sheng; his uncle Xi executed the entire Duan clan and usurped the imperial title.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month Duan Xing killed Murong Sheng; Xi his uncle wiped out the Duan clan and declared himself emperor.

sentences.zh: 冬十二月，集博士儒生比眾經文字，義類相從，凡四萬餘字，號曰《眾文經》。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter erudites and Confucian scholars were assembled to compare the written forms of the classics, arranging meanings by category, more than forty thousand characters in all, titled The Comprehensive Script Classic.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he gathered scholars to harmonize the written forms of the classics into more than forty thousand characters, called the Comprehensive Script Classic.

sentences.zh: 是歲，涼武昭王、沮渠蒙遜並遣使朝貢。

translations.literal: That year the Martial and Illustrious King of Liang and Juqu Mengxun both sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: That year the King of Liang and Juqu Mengxun both sent tribute missions.

sentences.zh: 五年春正月，帝聞姚興將寇邊，庚寅，大簡輿徒，詔并州諸軍積穀於平陽乾壁。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the fifth year, hearing that Yao Xing would raid the frontier, on day gengyin he conducted a great muster of carriage and foot levies and ordered the armies of Bing Province to store grain at Ganbi in Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, learning that Yao Xing meant to attack the border, on gengyin day he mustered the army and ordered Bingzhou troops to stock grain at Ganbi in Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 三月，禿發利鹿孤死。

translations.literal: In the third month Tufa Lilugu died.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Tufa Lilugu died.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，姚興遣其弟義陽王平來侵平陽，攻陷乾壁。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer Yao Xing sent his younger brother the Prince of Yiyang, Ping, to invade Pingyang and storm Ganbi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Yao Xing sent his brother the Prince of Yiyang to invade Pingyang and take Ganbi.

sentences.zh: 秋七月戊辰朔，車駕西討。

translations.literal: On the first day of the seventh month of autumn, day wuchen, the imperial carriage set out on a western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day, the new moon of the seventh month, the court marched west on campaign.

sentences.zh: 八月乙巳，至乾壁，平固守，進軍圍之。

translations.literal: On day yisi in the eighth month he reached Ganbi; Ping held firm, so the army advanced and besieged him.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day in the eighth month he reached Ganbi, besieged Ping where he held the fortress, and pressed the siege.

sentences.zh: 姚興悉舉其眾來救。

translations.literal: Yao Xing mustered his entire host to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing marched out with his whole army to relieve the siege.

sentences.zh: 甲子，帝度蒙坑，逆擊興軍大破之。

translations.literal: On day jiazi the Emperor crossed Meng Ravine and met Xing's army head-on, routing it utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi day the Emperor crossed Meng Ravine, met Yao Xing's army, and shattered it.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，平赴水而死，俘其餘眾三萬餘人，獲興尚書左僕射狄伯支以下四品將軍以上四十餘人。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter Ping threw himself into the water and died; more than thirty thousand of the remainder were captured, and Xing's Minister of the Masters of Writing, Left Vice Director Di Bozhi, and more than forty generals of the fourth rank and above were taken.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Ping drowned himself; more than thirty thousand survivors were captured along with Di Bozhi, Yao Xing's vice minister of the Masters of Writing, and more than forty generals of the fourth rank and above.

sentences.zh: 獲前亡臣王次多、靳勒，並斬以徇。

translations.literal: Former defectors Wang Ciduo and Jin Le were also seized and beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Former deserters Wang Ciduo and Jin Le were taken and beheaded before the army.

sentences.zh: 興頻使請和，帝不許。

translations.literal: Xing repeatedly sent envoys suing for peace; the Emperor would not consent.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Xing sued for peace again and again; the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 群臣請進平蒲阪，帝慮蠕蠕為難，戊申，班師。

translations.literal: The ministers asked to advance on Ping and Pu Ban; the Emperor feared trouble from the Rouran, and on day wushen withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: His ministers urged him to push on to Puban; fearing the Rouran, he withdrew on wushen day.

sentences.zh: 十一月，車駕次晉陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month the imperial carriage halted at Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month the court camped at Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 征相州刺史庾岳為司空。

translations.literal: Yu Yue, Inspector of Xiang Province, was summoned and made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Yu Yue, inspector of Xiangzhou, and made him Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 十二月辛亥，至自西征。

translations.literal: On day xinhai in the twelfth month he returned from the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai day in the twelfth month he returned from the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 越勒莫弗率其部萬餘家內屬。

translations.literal: Yuele Mofu led more than ten thousand households of his tribe to submit inward.
translations.idiomatic: Yuele Mofu brought more than ten thousand households of his tribe into allegiance.

sentences.zh: 六年春正月辛未，朔方尉遲部別帥率萬家內屬，入居雲中。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the sixth year, on day xinwei, a sub-chief of the Shuofang Yuchi division led ten thousand households to submit inward and settle in Yunzhong.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day in the first month of the sixth year a Yuchi chieftain of Shuofang led ten thousand families to submit and settle in Yunzhong.

sentences.zh: 夏四月癸巳朔，日有蝕之。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month of summer, day guisi, there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi day, the new moon of the fourth month, the sun was eclipsed.

sentences.zh: 五月，大簡輿徒，將略江淮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month a great muster of carriage and foot levies was held, intending to campaign against the Jiang and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he mustered a great army, intending to strike toward the Yangzi and Huai.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，鎮西大將軍、司隸校尉、毗陵王順有罪，以王還第。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Piling Prince Shun, Grand General Who Pacifies the West and Colonel Director of Retainers, was guilty of crime and sent back to his estate as a prince only.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Prince Shun of Piling, Grand General Who Pacifies the West and Director of Retainers, was found guilty and stripped to his princely estate.

sentences.zh: 戊子，北巡，築離宮於豺山，縱士校獵，東北逾罽嶺，出參合、代穀。

translations.literal: On day wuzi he toured north, built a detached palace on Wolf Mountain, let the soldiers hunt in competition, and went northeast beyond Ji Ridge, emerging by Canhe and Dai Valley.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi day he toured north, built a lodge on Wolf Mountain, held a competitive hunt, crossed Ji Ridge northeast, and came out through Canhe and Dai Valley.

sentences.zh: 九月，行幸南平城，規度氵壘南夏屋山，背黃瓜堆，將建新邑。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he traveled to Nanping city, surveyed Yongnan and Summer House Mountain, with Yellow Melon Mound at its back, intending to establish a new capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he went to Nanping city and surveyed Yongnan and Summer House Hill, backed by Yellow Melon Mound, planning a new capital.

sentences.zh: 辛未，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On day xinwei the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei day the court returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，起西昭陽殿。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter work began on the Western Zhaoyang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month work began on the Western Zhaoyang Hall.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，立皇子嗣為齊王，加車騎大將軍，位相國。

translations.literal: On day yimao the Emperor's son Si was established as Prince of Qi, promoted to Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, and given rank equal to the Chancellor of State.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao day he made his son Si Prince of Qi, Grand General of Chariots and Cavalry, with rank equal to the chancellor.

sentences.zh: 紹為清河王，加征南大將軍。

translations.literal: Shao was made Prince of Qinghe and promoted to Grand General Who Conquers the South.
translations.idiomatic: Shao became Prince of Qinghe and Grand General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 熙為陽平王，曜為河南王。

translations.literal: Xi was made Prince of Yangping and Yao Prince of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Xi became Prince of Yangping and Yao Prince of Henan.

sentences.zh: 封故秦湣王子夔為豫章王，陳留桓王子悅為硃提王。

translations.literal: Kui, son of the former Lamented King of Qin, was enfeoffed as Prince of Yuzhang, and Yue, son of the Prince of Chenliu Huan, as Prince of Zhuti.
translations.idiomatic: He enfeoffed Kui, son of the late King of Qin, as Prince of Yuzhang, and Yue, son of Prince Huan of Chenliu, as Prince of Zhuti.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，晉人來聘。

translations.literal: On day dingsi envoys came from Jin on a friendly mission.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi day Jin sent envoys on a friendly visit.

sentences.zh: 十一月庚午，將軍伊謂大破高車。

translations.literal: On day gengwu in the eleventh month General Yi Wei routed the Gaoche utterly.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu day in the eleventh month General Yi Wei shattered the Gaoche.

sentences.zh: 十二月，晉桓玄廢其主司馬德宗為平固王而自立，僭號楚。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month Huan Xuan of Jin deposed his lord Sima Dezong to Prince of Pinggu and set himself up, usurping the title King of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Huan Xuan of Jin deposed Emperor Dezong to Prince of Pinggu and made himself King of Chu.

sentences.zh: 天賜元年春二月，晉劉裕起兵誅桓玄。

translations.literal: In the second month of spring in the first year of Tianci, Liu Yu of Jin raised troops and executed Huan Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianci year one Liu Yu of Jin raised an army and killed Huan Xuan.

sentences.zh: 三月，初限縣戶不滿百罷之。

translations.literal: In the third month it was first ordered that counties with fewer than a hundred households be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he abolished every county with fewer than a hundred households.

sentences.zh: 夏五月，置山東諸冶，發州郡徒謫造兵甲。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer smelters were established throughout Shandong, and convict labor from the provinces and commanderies was levied to forge weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he set up foundries across Shandong and drafted convicts from every province to forge arms and armor.

sentences.zh: 秋九月，帝臨昭陽殿，分置眾職，引朝臣文武親自簡擢，量能敘用。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn the Emperor came to Zhaoyang Hall, divided and assigned the host of offices, and personally selected and promoted civil and military courtiers according to their capacity.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he sat in Zhaoyang Hall, reorganized the offices, and personally chose civil and military men according to their talents.

sentences.zh: 制爵四等，曰王、公、侯、子，除伯、男之號。

translations.literal: Noble ranks were fixed at four grades: king, duke, marquis, and viscount; the titles of earl and baron were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He fixed nobility at four ranks, king, duke, marquis, and viscount, and abolished the ranks of earl and baron.

sentences.zh: 追錄舊臣，加封爵各有差。

translations.literal: Former ministers were traced and recorded, with enfeoffments and titles added in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: He posthumously honored old ministers with titles and fiefs according to their service.

sentences.zh: 是秋，江南大亂，流人繦負奔淮北者行道相尋。

translations.literal: That autumn great disorder arose south of the Yangzi; refugees swaddled on the back filled the roads north of the Huai, one after another.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the south fell into chaos and refugees with infants on their backs filled the roads to the Huai north bank.

sentences.zh: 冬十月辛巳，大赦，改元。

translations.literal: On day xinsi in the tenth month of winter a great amnesty was proclaimed and the reign era changed.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi day in the tenth month he proclaimed a general amnesty and changed the era name.

sentences.zh: 築西宮。

translations.literal: The Western Palace was built.
translations.idiomatic: He built the Western Palace.

sentences.zh: 十一月，幸西宮，大選臣僚，令各辨宗党，保舉才行，諸部子孫失業賜爵者二千餘人。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he visited the Western Palace, made a great selection of officials, ordered each to distinguish his clan and lineage and recommend men of talent and conduct, and more than two thousand sons of the various departments who had lost office were granted noble rank.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he went to the Western Palace, had officials sort their clans and recommend talent, and ennobled more than two thousand idle sons of the departments.

sentences.zh: 二年春正月，晉主司馬德宗復位。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the second year the Jin ruler Sima Dezong was restored to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two Sima Dezong of Jin was restored to the throne.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，祀西郊，車旗盡黑。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer sacrifice was made at the western suburb; chariots and banners were all black.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he sacrificed at the western suburb with chariots and banners all in black.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，慕容德死。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of winter Murong De died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Murong De died.

sentences.zh: 三年春正月甲申，北巡，幸豺山宮，校獵，還至屋孤山。

translations.literal: In the first month of spring in the third year, on day jiashen, he toured north, visited Wolf Mountain Palace, held a competitive hunt, and returned to Wugu Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen day in the first month of year three he toured north to Wolf Mountain Palace, hunted, and returned to Wugu Mountain.

sentences.zh: 二月乙亥，幸代園山，建五石亭。

translations.literal: On day yihai he visited Dai Garden Mountain and built the Five Stone Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai day he went to Dai Garden Mountain and built the Five Stone Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 三月庚子，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On day gengzi the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi day the court returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 夏四月庚申，復幸豺山宮。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of summer, on day gengshen, he again visited Wolf Mountain Palace.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen day in the fourth month he again visited Wolf Mountain Palace.

sentences.zh: 占授著作郎王宜弟造《兵法孤虛立成圖》三百六十。

translations.literal: By divination the Attendant Gentleman Wang Yidi was appointed to compose three hundred sixty diagrams of military methods, void and solitary formations, and standing completion.
translations.idiomatic: By divination he appointed Attendant Gentleman Wang Yidi to compose three hundred sixty charts of void formations and military method.

sentences.zh: 時遂登定襄角史山，又幸馬城。

translations.literal: At the time he then ascended Dingxiang Horn Historian Mountain and also visited Horse City.
translations.idiomatic: He then climbed Dingxiang Horn Historian Mountain and visited Horse City.

sentences.zh: 甲戌，車駕還宮。

translations.literal: On day jiaxu the imperial carriage returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day the court returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 六月，發八部五百里內男丁築氵壘南宮，門闕高十餘丈。

translations.literal: In the sixth month adult males within five hundred li of the eight tribes were levied to build the Yongnan Palace; gate towers rose more than ten zhang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he drafted men from the eight tribes within five hundred li to build the Yongnan Palace with gate towers more than ten zhang high.

sentences.zh: 引溝穿池，廣苑囿。

translations.literal: Channels were cut and pools dug to enlarge the parks and preserves.
translations.idiomatic: He cut canals, dug pools, and enlarged the imperial parks.

sentences.zh: 規立外城方二十里，分置市里，經途洞達。

translations.literal: An outer wall twenty li square was planned, markets and wards were set out, and thoroughfares ran through without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: He planned an outer city twenty li square with wards and markets and straight streets running through.

sentences.zh: 三十日罷。

translations.literal: After thirty days the work was halted.
translations.idiomatic: After thirty days the labor was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，太尉穆崇薨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn Grand Commandant Mu Chong died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Grand Commandant Mu Chong died.

sentences.zh: 八月甲辰，行幸豺山宮，遂至青牛山。

translations.literal: On day jiachen he traveled to Wolf Mountain Palace and then reached Green Ox Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen day he went to Wolf Mountain Palace and then to Green Ox Mountain.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，西登武要北原，觀九十九泉，造古亭，遂之石漠。

translations.literal: On day bingchen he climbed west to the northern plain of Wuyao, viewed the ninety-nine springs, built an ancient-style pavilion, and then went on to Stone Desert.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen day he climbed the northern plain of Wuyao westward, viewed the ninety-nine springs, built a pavilion in the old style, and went on to Stone Desert.

sentences.zh: 九月甲戌朔，幸漠南鹽池。

translations.literal: On the first day of the ninth month, day jiaxu, he visited the salt pools south of the desert.
